proposed_title: Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work
description: Read maps, charts, dashboards, model outputs and monitoring summaries correctly; identify what was measured, where, when, by whom and at what resolution; recognize the limits of a data product before relying on it; ask the questions that expose misuse (scale, sample, baseline, missing data).
rationale: Tier DC-1 (universal). v1 has no universal data-literacy competency; data skills are scattered across Domain 2 as tool competencies that most practitioners will never hold at Intermediate. The Five Functional Positions critical competency 'knowing what the analysis can't tell you' (DC-044) belongs to everyone who consumes evidence, not only analysts. Plans demand interpretation of long-lived authoritative data (ROS, NRV, hydrologic modeling, FIA, SSURGO; DC-035).

proposed_title: Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work
description: Choose whether and how to use a general-purpose or embedded AI tool for a work task; give it adequate context; check outputs for accuracy, completeness and appropriateness before acting; keep sensitive and controlled information out of unapproved tools; disclose AI involvement in work products; follow agency or employer AI rules.
rationale: Tier DC-1 (universal). Enterprise GenAI assistants are deployed agency-wide with training (OPM, DC-013; USGS Azure OpenAI, NOAA Gemini, EPA Azure OpenAI in DC-001). DOL TEN 07-25 (2026-02-13) makes AI literacy a public-workforce-system expectation (DC-015) with content areas that map to observable behavior (DC-016). EU Art. 4 still requires deployers to take literacy measures after the 2026 Omnibus (DC-017). SC secondary because rule-following and disclosure are institutional obligations. Competency text must not name tools or memos (they live in the tools layer).

proposed_title: Design monitoring and sampling for valid environmental inference
description: Specify monitoring questions, indicators, sampling frames, sample sizes and detection methods (field crews, sensors, remote sensing, eDNA, acoustic, citizen science) so that results support the inferences and decisions they are meant to inform, including power to detect change and how imperfect detection is handled.
rationale: Monitoring is the single largest structured data demand in land-management plans (3,843 monitoring components, DC-035) yet v1 has no competency for monitoring design as such; it is implied in 1.1.2 T1 and scattered in Domain 4. AI detectors and new sensors change what can be counted cheaply, which makes design (what to sample, how to handle detection error) more, not less, important. FC secondary: indicator selection and site representativeness require field judgment (v1 rule on liberal FC-sec for DC-primary, DC-043).

proposed_title: Engineer environmental sensor-network and streaming data pipelines
description: Design and operate the data path from deployed sensors, telemetry, cameras and recorders to analysis-ready data: ingest, time synchronization, automated QC and anomaly flags, gap handling, storage, versioning and alerting, including edge processing where bandwidth is limited.
rationale: Inventories show AI QC of water-level and ocean observations, edge-AI survey payloads, robotic microscopes and coastal modeling sandboxes at NOAA and sensor-stream QC at USGS/USDA (DC-001). v1 splits this across 2.3.1 (deployment) and 2.6.4 (AI QC) and treats it as tool use; it is a durable engineering capability. Field deployment and calibration stay FC-led (split recommended in v1_assessment).

proposed_title: Document data provenance and lineage for environmental evidence
description: Record and preserve where each dataset and derived product came from: sources and versions, collection methods, transformations, models and AI systems involved (with versions and prompts where relevant), human review steps and responsible parties, so that any finding can be traced, reproduced or corrected.
rationale: Machine-generated text, metadata and maps now enter administrative records. In the 2024 inventory only 37% of USDA AI use cases reported complete or widely available training/evaluation-data documentation, 26% partial, 15% missing and 22% unreported (DC-002). The CEQ NEPA and Permitting Data and Technology Standard v1.2 added record-origin and record-version fields (DC-034). M-26-04 requires model/system/data cards for procured LLMs (DC-008). SC secondary: provenance is what makes an analysis defensible in the administrative record. v1 has QC (2.2.3) and metadata (2.2.5) but no provenance/lineage competency.

proposed_title: Steward and publish environmental data for reuse
description: Prepare datasets for discovery and reuse by others: apply metadata and vocabulary standards, choose repositories, licenses and persistent identifiers, document fitness for use, run sensitivity review before release, and review machine-generated metadata for accuracy rather than authoring it from scratch.
rationale: v1 2.2.5 is classified Ac/Ac/V with CLD-Moderate (DC-046): metadata authoring is being automated (USDA NRCS DS Hub generative metadata, DC-001). The durable capability is stewardship judgment: what fitness-for-use a user needs and whether released data are safe and correctly licensed. FAIR (DC-049, unverified this session) and open-data law (DC-052, unverified) are durable principles; specific templates and tools go to the tools layer.

proposed_title: Protect sensitive ecological, cultural and personal information in data products
description: Determine and document the sensitivity of species locations, archaeological and cultural sites, Tribal information and personal data; apply generalization, withholding or controlled access proportionate to the risk; never alter the stored record; record reasons and review dates; check derived products (maps, model outputs, AI summaries, training sets) for leakage.
rationale: GBIF guidance gives explicit, observable practices: a documented reason and review date for every sensitivity call, generalization to 0.1 or 0.01 degrees by category, restricting only distributed copies (DC-029). OpenLMP's never-publish list (DC-036) is a working example. Risk rises with AI: training sets, embeddings and summaries can leak locations that redacted tables do not. Indigenous data governance itself is owned by TN/SC (v1 7.1.1, CARE DC-050); this competency is the technical execution layer and must be co-designed with TN. Absent from v1 except as a records-management task (3.3.5 T2).

proposed_title: Conduct reproducible, auditable environmental analysis, including AI-assisted code
description: Carry out analyses as re-runnable workflows (scripted or fully documented steps, version control, recorded environments and inputs), test and review code including code generated by AI assistants, and package analyses so a peer or auditor can reproduce results.
rationale: v1 2.2.4 'Programming and scripting' carries the taxonomy's CLD-High finding: AI code generation compresses the practice that builds debugging capacity (DC-046). Inventories show code assistants in production use (GitHub Copilot, Gemini Code Assist, Amazon Q, 'ChatGPT to write Python scripts for ArcGIS Pro', code translation Matlab/R/Python; DC-001) and PermitAI benchmarks coding agents for NEPA drafting (DC-032). The durable competency is reproducibility and review, not language fluency; languages go to the tools layer. Assessment can require reproducing someone else's analysis and finding a planted defect.

proposed_title: Evaluate model fitness-for-purpose and validate against independent evidence
description: Judge whether a statistical, process, machine-learning or AI model is fit for a stated decision: check assumptions and domain of applicability, design independent validation (held-out, spatially/temporally blocked, field reference data), quantify error by condition, detect out-of-distribution use and document limits.
rationale: NOAA inventory entries such as 'Predictability of Species Distributions Deteriorates Under Novel Environmental Conditions' and 'Uncertainties and recommendations for projecting species distributions under climate change' (DC-001) show validation under non-analog conditions is live practice. OPM's AI model lists 'Testing and Validation' as a technical competency (DC-012); AI RMF names 'valid and reliable' first among trustworthiness characteristics (DC-005). EPA's 2009 model guidance (DC-051) and banking SR 11-7 (DC-059) are durable precedents (not re-read this session). v1 embeds validation inside tasks (2.6.1 T3, 2.1.2 T3) but has no stand-alone model evaluation competency.

proposed_title: Apply Earth-observation foundation models and learned embeddings to environmental mapping
description: Select, fine-tune or use pre-computed embeddings from EO foundation models for classification, regression and change detection; design reference data and accuracy assessment; test transfer to local ecosystems; account for training-data circularity (e.g., models trained on the same products they are used to update) and for limited interpretability.
rationale: Prithvi-EO-2.0 (2024-12, DC-023), OlmoEarth v1/v1.1/v1.2 within about a year (DC-025), Clay (DC-024) and Google's AlphaEarth Satellite Embedding V1 (DC-028) are operational; USGS reports a 'Foundation Models to Advance Earth Science' pilot and deploys deep learning for NLCD change mapping (DC-001). The Earth Engine catalog states embedding bands are 'not independently interpretable' and were trained with NLCD and CDL targets (DC-028), so validation independence is a real, testable skill. The specific models have half-lives of 1-3 years (tools layer); the competency (transfer testing, reference design, circularity awareness) is durable.

proposed_title: Quantify and communicate uncertainty for environmental decisions
description: Characterize uncertainty from measurement, sampling, model structure, parameters, scenarios and AI error; express it in forms decision-makers can use (ranges, probabilities, confidence language, maps of confidence); state what would change the conclusion; resist pressure to drop caveats.
rationale: NWCG FBAN/LTAN standards require communicating 'uncertainty and confidence' (per DC-047, unverified citations). M-26-04 requires procured LLMs to 'acknowledge uncertainty' (DC-008) - the human analyst must at least meet that bar. Only 38 of 58,544 plan components mention uncertainty (DC-035), suggesting it is under-specified in demand documents. In v1 uncertainty appears only inside indicators and tasks (1.6.2 T2, 2.2.2 T3). SC secondary: how uncertainty is framed for authorizing officials is a statecraft act.

proposed_title: Build, run and validate environmental forecast systems and digital twins
description: Assemble observation streams, models (process-based, AI emulators or hybrids), data assimilation and update cycles into forecast or what-if systems; define fitness for the decisions they serve; validate continuously; manage versions and communicate when the system should not be trusted.
rationale: NOAA's inventory includes an AI-driven global forecast model and ensemble, an Ai2 Climate Emulator (ACE) collaboration, a 'Digital Twin for Earth Observations Using AI' pilot, physics-informed neural networks and hybrid physics-ML precipitation models (DC-001). v1 2.7.3 treats digital twins as an immersive technology; the durable capability is model-data fusion and validation. NASA ESDT and DestinE (DC-054, DC-055) could not be verified this session.

proposed_title: Validate AI-generated environmental analyses before professional use
description: Check AI-produced species identifications, maps, classifications, summaries, regulatory analyses and drafts against independent evidence (field observation, source documents, legal text, expert knowledge); use structured sampling when volumes are large; record what was checked, what was changed and the confidence of the validation.
rationale: Rewrite and promotion of v1 7.2.1, the strongest data-craft competency in v1 (DC-045). Evidence that validation is the real job: FWS DocketScope states 'Results are verified by analysts during comment review'; BLM's AIM chatbot directs that responses are 'strictly for information gathering'; USDA's permitting triage routes non-CE cases to 'more human intervention' (DC-001). DOL lists 'Evaluating AI outputs' as a core content area (DC-016). Change from v1: add statistical sampling for high-volume outputs, make documentation of validation an observable product, and keep FC secondary for ecological outputs.

proposed_title: Design human-in-the-loop review for AI-assisted environmental workflows
description: Specify where people review, approve or override AI outputs in a workflow: risk-based review rates, confidence thresholds and escalation triggers, reviewer qualifications, independence from the tool's producer, audit logs, and measures that show whether review is substantive rather than rubber-stamp.
rationale: M-25-21 requires human oversight and intervention safeguards for high-impact AI (DC-007). Deployed environmental tools rely on analyst verification (DC-001). Three environmental use cases (USDA environmental permitting review, USDA dam-inspection document processing, an EPA OECA video tool) were 'presumed high-impact' but determined not high-impact because AI 'is not making any final decisions, only recommendations for authorized staff to review' (DC-001): whether review is substantive is what the designation actually hinges on. v1 places 'design human-in-the-loop oversight architectures' as a task inside 7.1.4 (SC primary, no DC secondary; DC-045); the design of review sampling and thresholds is an analytical specification that needs DC capacity, while authorizing the design stays SC. Distinct from DC-CAND-13 (doing validation) and DC-CAND-19 (deciding risk tier).

proposed_title: Build task-specific evaluation sets and benchmark AI tools before adoption
description: Construct a representative, independently labeled reference set for a specific environmental task; measure candidate tools (precision, recall, error by subgroup or condition, citation accuracy) against it and against the current human process; document results so adoption, procurement and monitoring decisions rest on local evidence.
rationale: OpenLMP's blind gold set with kappa 0.939 (DC-037), PNNL's DraftNEPABench with SME rubrics graded by LLM judges (DC-032), GEO-Bench for EO models (DC-060) and NIST Dioptra for second-party testing (DC-041) show the practice exists. The 2025 inventory asks whether high-impact AI had testing conducted (DC-001). Vendor benchmarks rarely match local ecosystems or document types, so this is the main defence against both over- and under-trust. Distinct from v1 7.2.3 (individual calibration) - this is an organizational evidence product.

proposed_title: Analyze regulatory, planning and public-comment text with LLMs, with traceable citations
description: Use LLM-based extraction, classification and summarization on plans, environmental documents, permits, biological opinions and public comments; require every extracted statement to trace to a source passage; measure omission and fabrication rates; keep the legal sufficiency judgment with the responsible official.
rationale: This is where environmental GenAI is actually deployed: USFS 'Forest Plan review and planning support' and 'Turbo plan' (deployed 2025), FWS DocketScope (deployed), EPA Region 8 comment summarization (pilot), USDA public-comment analysis, BLM GraphRAG comment analysis and NEPA document generation, BLM 'RUDD' small language model for planning decisions, NOAA 'Generative AI for Biological Opinions' and CZMA 312 evaluation pilot (DC-001); PermitAI services and benchmarks (DC-032, DC-033). DOI's PCAT and I-NEPA tools were retired between inventories (DC-001), showing tool churn. Planned v1 7.2.4-7.2.5 were never drafted; this fills that gap. SC secondary: the output enters an administrative record.

proposed_title: Supervise agentic AI workflows in environmental analysis
description: Scope tasks delegated to AI agents that plan and take multi-step actions (retrieve data, run tools, write code, draft documents); set permissions and stop conditions; insert checkpoints; review action logs; detect silent failure; and take responsibility for the result.
rationale: Of 438 USDA/DOI/EPA use cases in the 2025 inventory, 8 are classed agentic; the 2 deployed are administrative (grants utility, supply-chain security), and environmental ones are pilots or pre-deployment (NRCS automated waterway design, BLM 'AI Trapline for Fire', USGS DiscoverDOI) (DC-001). PNNL benchmarks coding agents drafting EIS sections (DC-032). Labeled S: the need is plausible and growing but environmental deployments are not yet evidenced; confirm by tracking the 2026 inventory and PermitAI adoption. Keep emergent tier; review annually.

proposed_title: Curate authoritative knowledge corpora for retrieval-augmented AI
description: Select, version and maintain the documents, protocols, datasets and metadata that AI assistants retrieve from; mark authority, currency and supersession; remove withdrawn guidance; test retrieval quality; and assign ownership so assistants answer from the current, authoritative source.
rationale: Retrieval chatbots over agency corpora are among the most common environmental GenAI pilots: BLM AIM chatbot over 73,000+ monitoring locations' guidance, FVS helpdesk RAG, USDA ASKTERRA and GIS help desk bots, NOAA Storm Events knowledge-graph chatbot (DC-001). Answer quality depends on corpus curation more than on the model. Rewrites v1 2.5.4 'Knowledge management systems' (a platform competency) into a durable stewardship capability.

proposed_title: Assess and manage model risk for consequential environmental decisions
description: Maintain an inventory of models and AI systems that inform decisions; tier them by consequence (e.g., effect on payments, permits, enforcement, safety, rights, cultural resources); set proportional requirements for validation, documentation, independent review, monitoring and retirement; and decide when a model must not be used.
rationale: Excluding a facial-recognition security system, the only high-impact AI in USDA/DOI/EPA's 2025 inventory are satellite-and-crop-model mapping to verify farm-program reporting (USDA Farm Production and Conservation cover crop mapping and planting date detection, pre-deployment; acreage and crop type validation) and EPA enforcement uses (deployed RCRA large-quantity-generator inspection risk scoring; TSCA document review) (DC-001): EO and ML models become 'high-impact' when they drive payments or enforcement, not when they are technically novel. M-25-21 defines high-impact AI and minimum practices (DC-007). Environmental organizations have no equivalent of banking model-risk management (DC-059) [J]. SC secondary: deciding a tier is partly a governance call, but it rests on technical evaluation that v1 7.1.4 delegates away.

proposed_title: Specify, evaluate and accept AI and analytics services in procurement
description: Write requirements and acceptance tests for AI/analytics services; require model and data documentation, data-rights terms (no training on government or partner data without consent), portability and exit provisions, performance monitoring and change notification; evaluate vendor claims against a local evaluation set.
rationale: M-25-22 requires contract terms preventing vendors training on government data, data/model portability, and ongoing performance monitoring (DC-007); M-26-04 requires acceptable-use policies, model/system/data cards and user feedback channels for every procured LLM (DC-008). Many deployed environmental tools are vendor-built (Google for USFS plan review, Wildfire.org for Turbo plan, The Regulatory Group for DocketScope; DC-001). Contracting officers cannot judge model documentation alone; v1 3.3.4/3.1.4 cover procurement without any AI content.

proposed_title: Govern enterprise environmental data and AI portfolios
description: Set and run organizational data and AI strategy: data governance bodies and stewardship roles, data catalog and inventory, data-sharing agreements, AI use-case inventory and determinations, workforce data/AI capability, and measures of data and AI value and risk.
rationale: Tier DC-4. M-25-21 requires CAIOs and AI governance boards with data representation (DC-007); EPA runs AI governance inside its Data Governance Advisory Committee (DC-022); OPM uses AI Impact Assessments on data and cataloging practices (DC-013); in 2024, 172 of 180 DOI and all 89 USDA use cases reported access to an enterprise data catalog (DC-002). The CDO function (Evidence Act, DC-052 unverified) is the durable anchor. v1 has no enterprise data governance competency; 7.1.4 is AI-only and SC-only.

proposed_title: Design decision-support products for actual decision contexts
description: Build maps, dashboards, scenario tools and briefings around the real decision, its timing, authority and constraints; test with decision-makers; show trade-offs and uncertainty; and evaluate whether the product changed or improved decisions.
rationale: Rewrite of v1 2.4.3 (tool-framed 'use decision support tools ... build dashboards'). The Five Functional Positions critical competency 'designing for actual decision contexts, not idealized ones' (DC-044) is durable; dashboards and DSS software (EMDS, deployed since 1997 per DC-001) belong to the tools layer. Absorbs durable parts of 2.7.4 immersive visualization.

proposed_title: Operate and optimize drinking water treatment processes to meet regulatory and aesthetic targets
description: Controls source-to-finished-water treatment (coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, disinfection, corrosion control) by reading plant conditions, running process tests (e.g., jar tests, CT calculations, turbidity trending), adjusting setpoints and documenting decisions. Observable: shift logs, process-control decisions under changing raw water, compliance results, response to upsets.
rationale: Core licensed-operator competency with no v1 equivalent; certification grade ladders already define observable levels. Fieldcraft here is process-plant sensory judgment, not landscape craft (see report section 3.3).

proposed_title: Operate and optimize wastewater treatment and resource-recovery processes
description: Manages biological and physical-chemical treatment (activated sludge control, nutrient removal, solids handling, digestion/biosolids, energy recovery) to permit limits; interprets lab and online data; responds to upsets (toxic loads, wet weather). Observable: process-control records, permit compliance, upset response.
rationale: No v1 equivalent; wastewater operators are among the largest environmental occupations by headcount (51-8031, shared with W01).

proposed_title: Supervise automated and AI-assisted process control in environmental operations
description: Governs setpoints, alarms and automated control loops (SCADA, model-predictive or AI optimization) in plants and networks: defines override criteria, validates recommendations against process knowledge, runs safe manual operation when automation fails, and documents accountability as operator in responsible charge.
rationale: v1 Human-AI practice (7.2) is analysis-centric; operations need a control-room analog: the "can you still run it by hand" competency that protects tacit plant knowledge as automation spreads.

proposed_title: Interpret and apply drinking water compliance requirements
description: Determines which SDWA requirements apply to a system (monitoring schedules, MCLs/treatment techniques, lead and copper requirements incl. service-line inventories, PFAS, public notification, consumer confidence reports), tracks compliance, and prepares required reports. Observable: correct applicability determinations, compliant monitoring plans, timely notices.
rationale: Regulator and utility both need it; state primacy staff and utility compliance managers move between these roles. Rule timelines changed 2025-26 - content must be versioned against dated driver events.

proposed_title: Manage utility assets and capital plans using risk-based asset management
description: Builds and maintains asset inventories, condition and criticality assessments, CMMS work-order systems, level-of-service targets, and long-term capital/financial plans (rates, reserves, funding applications). Observable: asset registers, risk matrices, capital improvement plans, SRF or grant applications.
rationale: Technical-managerial-financial capacity is the main determinant of small-system compliance [J]; absent in v1 except generic equipment/asset management.

proposed_title: Protect operational technology at environmental utilities and facilities
description: Applies OT cybersecurity basics in plant and network operations: asset/network segmentation awareness, secure remote access, recognizing and reporting anomalous control behavior, incident response and manual fallback. Observable: completed risk assessments, response drills, corrected vulnerabilities.
rationale: Cyber incidents at water utilities are a recognized federal concern [J; verify]; operators, not only IT staff, must hold this competency.

proposed_title: Write and administer discharge permits
description: Develops NPDES/state discharge permits: characterizes the discharge and receiving water, derives technology-based and water-quality-based effluent limits (reasonable potential analysis), sets monitoring and special conditions, prepares fact sheets, responds to comments, and reviews DMRs for compliance. Observable: defensible permit and fact sheet; correct limit derivations.
rationale: Permit writing is a core state-agency job with a distinct technical-legal craft; v1 6.1.3 is applicant-side and generic. Mirror skill exists in permittee/consultant roles (mobility path).

proposed_title: Develop TMDLs and watershed-based restoration plans
description: Quantifies pollutant loads and capacity of impaired waters, allocates loads among point and nonpoint sources with margin of safety, and builds implementation and monitoring plans with stakeholders. Observable: TMDL report, model documentation, allocation rationale, implementation plan.
rationale: v1 has the science but not the regulatory product.

proposed_title: Inspect, verify and maintain stormwater control measures over their lifecycle
description: Conducts construction erosion and sediment control inspections, verifies post-construction stormwater control measures and green infrastructure function, directs maintenance and enforcement within MS4 programs. Observable: inspection reports, corrective actions, maintenance verification records.
rationale: v1 covers installation/maintenance but not the regulatory inspection and MS4 program side that local governments are permitted for.

proposed_title: Plan water supply and allocation under hydrologic uncertainty
description: Forecasts demand and supply, prepares drought contingency and integrated resource plans, applies water-rights or allocation rules, evaluates conjunctive use and reuse options. Observable: supply-demand analysis, drought plan, allocation decision record.
rationale: Water supply planning and water-rights administration are large state functions absent in v1.

proposed_title: Characterize groundwater systems and protect drinking water sources
description: Designs and interprets aquifer tests, well logs and groundwater monitoring; delineates wellhead/source-water protection areas; evaluates contaminant transport; applies UIC and well-construction requirements. Observable: conceptual hydrogeologic model, protection-area delineation, monitoring design.
rationale: No v1 groundwater competency.

proposed_title: Write and review air permits for stationary sources
description: Determines applicability (NSR/PSD, Title V, minor source, NESHAP), reviews emissions calculations and control technology (BACT/LAER/MACT) analyses, drafts enforceable permit conditions with monitoring/recordkeeping, and manages public notice. Observable: permit with defensible applicability and enforceable conditions.
rationale: Air permit engineering is the largest professional job in state/local air programs [J] and has no v1 competency; v1 6.7.5 is tagged S2/NEPA.

proposed_title: Operate and quality-assure ambient air monitoring networks, including sensor data
description: Sites, operates, calibrates and audits regulatory monitors; validates data against QA criteria; collocates and corrects low-cost sensors and integrates satellite products while keeping regulatory and non-regulatory data distinct. Observable: QA records, audit results, validated data sets, sensor correction documentation.
rationale: Sensor and satellite data are changing monitoring now [J]; the durable competency is QA judgment about data fitness for regulatory vs community use.

proposed_title: Build emissions inventories and air quality models for attainment planning
description: Compiles point, area, mobile and natural source inventories, runs or reviews dispersion and photochemical models, and develops control strategies and SIP demonstrations. Observable: inventory documentation, modeling protocol, attainment demonstration.
rationale: Distinct technical product absent in v1.

proposed_title: Plan smoke management that reconciles prescribed fire and air quality rules
description: Coordinates burn windows, smoke dispersion forecasts, exceptional-event documentation, public health messaging and interagency approvals between fire managers and air regulators. Observable: smoke management plan, approved burn day decisions, exceptional event packages.
rationale: Bridges v1 strength (fire) and gap (air); smoke/air terms appear in 373 forest-plan components [E: DB-011].

proposed_title: Manage solid waste collection, processing and disposal systems
description: Plans and operates collection, transfer, materials recovery, organics processing and landfill systems (cell operations, cover, leachate and gas control, contamination management), meeting permits and diversion goals. Observable: operating plans, compliance records, diversion and contamination metrics.
rationale: v1 treats waste as corporate circular-economy strategy; municipal and private waste operations are absent.

proposed_title: Administer extended producer responsibility and materials-management programs
description: Implements state EPR and materials-management laws: producer responsibility organization oversight, program plan review, needs assessments, performance targets, eco-modulated fees and reporting audits. Observable: approved program plans, audit findings, performance reports.
rationale: New state function created by EPR laws since 2021 [J; verify list].

proposed_title: Determine hazardous waste status and manage generator compliance
description: Makes waste determinations (listed/characteristic), manages accumulation, labeling, manifesting, land disposal restrictions and universal waste; prepares contingency plans and trains staff. Observable: documented determinations, compliant accumulation areas, manifests, inspection outcomes.
rationale: RCRA compliance is a core EHS function with no v1 coverage.

proposed_title: Conduct environmental site assessment and site characterization
description: Performs Phase I (records, reconnaissance, interviews) and Phase II assessments; designs sampling; builds and updates conceptual site models across media; evaluates data usability. Observable: AAI-conformant Phase I, sampling and analysis plan, CSM.
rationale: Entry point into the remediation profession; Phase I records review is a likely AI-compression task (role_signals).

proposed_title: Select, design and oversee remedies and long-term stewardship
description: Evaluates remedial alternatives against regulatory criteria, selects and designs remedies, oversees implementation and optimization, and manages institutional controls, five-year reviews and closure. Observable: feasibility study, decision document, O&M and LTS plans.
rationale: Federal facility cleanup (DoD/DOE) and state programs depend on it; absent in v1.

proposed_title: Investigate and manage emerging contaminants across media
description: Plans and interprets investigations for contaminants with evolving standards (e.g., PFAS): source identification, analytical method limits, risk communication under changing criteria, interim response and treatment selection. Observable: investigation plan, data interpretation memo, public communication.
rationale: Cross-media emerging work; standards changing 2024-26 makes it a test case for dated driver events.

proposed_title: Evaluate chemical hazards and risks under chemical regulatory programs
description: Assesses hazard, exposure and risk for chemical and pesticide decisions (TSCA risk evaluation, pesticide registration review, state chemical programs), including new approach methods and alternatives assessment. Observable: risk evaluation sections, weight-of-evidence documentation.
rationale: v1 has toxicology science but not regulatory chemical management.

proposed_title: Certify, inspect and enforce pesticide use
description: Runs or participates in state pesticide programs: applicator certification and recertification, use and misuse investigations, label-compliance inspections, worker protection. Observable: inspection and investigation reports, certification program records.
rationale: State agriculture departments are a large, overlooked environmental regulator.

proposed_title: Conduct multimedia compliance inspections and build enforceable case records
description: Plans risk-based inspections, gathers and preserves evidence (sampling, photos, records, interviews) with chain of custody, determines violations, writes inspection reports and supports enforcement or compliance assistance. Observable: inspection report and case file that survive legal review.
rationale: The inspector is the most common regulator-side environmental job [J]; v1 6.1.5 is generic "enforcement procedures".

proposed_title: Target and verify compliance with data analytics and remote monitoring
description: Uses e-reporting data, continuous monitoring, remote sensing and statistical targeting to prioritize inspections and detect noncompliance, while documenting limits and bias of the methods. Observable: targeting model documentation, validated detection-to-inspection outcomes.
rationale: Shrinking inspection capacity plus new sensing make targeting a growth competency [J].

proposed_title: Run a facility environmental management system and compliance calendar
description: Translates permits and rules into tasks, owners and deadlines; operates an EMS (ISO 14001 or equivalent); manages EPCRA/TRI, SPCC and other reporting; conducts internal audits and corrective action. Observable: compliance register, audit findings closed, on-time reports.
rationale: The regulated-entity side of every environmental program; absent in v1.

proposed_title: Conduct risk-based environmental public health inspections
description: Inspects food establishments, onsite wastewater systems, private wells, recreational water, institutions and housing against codes; prioritizes by risk; educates operators; documents and follows up violations. Observable: inspection reports, risk-factor findings, corrective action outcomes.
rationale: Core local health department job with no v1 equivalent.

proposed_title: Investigate environmental health complaints, outbreaks and emerging hazards
description: Investigates complaints and outbreaks (foodborne, waterborne, vector-borne, harmful algal blooms, heat, mold) with epidemiologists and labs: hypothesis-driven field investigation, sampling, control measures, reporting. Observable: investigation report, implemented controls, after-action review.
rationale: Climate is increasing this workload [J].

proposed_title: Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty
description: Designs and delivers risk and crisis communication (advisories, do-not-drink notices, cleanup updates, smoke and heat messaging) that is accurate, timely and trusted by affected publics, including in multiple languages. Observable: message maps, advisory products, audience comprehension testing.
rationale: v1 communication competencies are educational/interpretive; risk communication is a distinct, assessable skill.

proposed_title: Site and permit utility-scale clean energy and storage projects
description: Screens constraints, designs and interprets wildlife, wetland and cultural surveys, minimizes impacts (micro-siting, curtailment), assembles permits across federal, state and local authorities, and plans decommissioning and restoration. Observable: siting study, permit package, mitigation and decommissioning plans.
rationale: Distinct practice with heavy state siting role; demand volatile after 2025 federal incentive changes.

proposed_title: Manage environmental compliance for linear infrastructure and rights-of-way
description: Implements environmental conditions during construction and operation of transmission lines, pipelines and similar corridors (environmental inspection, spill and erosion control, sensitive-resource avoidance) and runs integrated vegetation management including wildfire mitigation clearances. Observable: inspection logs, IVM plans, compliance outcomes.
rationale: Utility vegetation management is a large field workforce [E: 55,160 tree trimmers, DB-001] and a wildfire-risk lever.

proposed_title: Detect, quantify and repair fugitive methane and VOC emissions
description: Plans and conducts leak detection (OGI, Method 21, continuous and remote/satellite detection), quantifies emissions, manages repair and reporting, and evaluates detection technologies. Observable: survey records, repair verification, emissions reports.
rationale: Shift from walk-down surveys to alert response; federal rule status volatile - state programs persist [J].

proposed_title: Plug orphaned and abandoned wells and restore sites
description: Inventories and prioritizes orphaned wells, plans and oversees plugging, measures pre/post emissions, and restores surface sites. Observable: prioritized inventory, plugging records, restoration verification.
rationale: New public workforce created by IIJA funding [J].

proposed_title: Plan and implement mine reclamation and abandoned mine land remediation
description: Develops reclamation plans and bonds, oversees regrading, revegetation and water treatment (including acid mine drainage), evaluates bond release, and runs AML hazard abatement projects. Observable: reclamation plan, bond calculation, bond-release inspection, AML project close-out.
rationale: Minerals/mining/reclamation appear in 1,377 forest-plan components [E: DB-011]; v1 has only sector-note mentions.

proposed_title: Measure and verify energy and emissions performance of facilities and buildings
description: Conducts energy audits, benchmarking and measurement and verification; supports building performance standard compliance and decarbonization plans. Observable: audit report, M&V plan and results, benchmarking submissions.
rationale: State/local building performance standards create public-sector demand [J].

proposed_title: Prepare and verify greenhouse gas inventories for organizations and jurisdictions
description: Defines boundaries, collects activity data, applies emission factors and methods (GHG Protocol, ISO 14064, government inventory guidance), quantifies uncertainty, documents data quality and prepares for verification or assurance. Observable: inventory with methods, QA/QC and verifiable audit trail.
rationale: v1 6.6.1 is land/market carbon; organizational and jurisdictional inventories are the main climate job [J].

proposed_title: Develop and track climate action plans with measurable emissions pathways
description: Builds emissions baselines and scenarios, selects and sequences policies and programs, estimates reductions and co-benefits, and tracks implementation with public reporting. Observable: plan with quantified pathways, tracking dashboard, progress reports.
rationale: State and local climate offices perform this; absent in v1.

proposed_title: Integrate climate risk into infrastructure and capital decisions
description: Applies climate projections to design criteria, asset vulnerability and capital prioritization (resilience benefit-cost, adaptation pathways) for utilities, transportation and facilities. Observable: climate-adjusted design basis, vulnerability assessment, prioritized capital list.
rationale: v1 adaptation is ecosystem-focused; infrastructure is where most adaptation spending occurs [J].

proposed_title: Plan and run extreme heat preparedness and response programs
description: Maps heat vulnerability, coordinates cooling resources, alerts and outreach, workplace and outdoor-worker protections, and evaluates outcomes with health partners. Observable: heat plan, activation records, after-action evaluation.
rationale: New local function [J]; links EH, EM and planning.

proposed_title: Develop hazard mitigation plans and fundable mitigation projects
description: Conducts hazard and risk assessments, builds mitigation strategies with stakeholders, scopes projects, and prepares benefit-cost analyses and applications for federal, state and other funding (program availability shifted in 2025-26; verify). Observable: adopted hazard mitigation plan, scoped projects with BCA.
rationale: Mitigation planning is a statutory local/state function with no v1 equivalent.

proposed_title: Conduct environmental and historic preservation review for disaster recovery and mitigation
description: Reviews disaster recovery and mitigation projects for NEPA, ESA, NHPA, floodplain/wetland and other requirements under compressed timelines; documents compliance and conditions. Observable: EHP review records, conditions, consultation outcomes.
rationale: Large temporary federal/contract workforce after disasters; bridges v1 NEPA strength into EM.

proposed_title: Coordinate environmental response operations within incident command
description: Plans and executes environmental response roles under ICS/NIMS (ESF-10 hazmat, debris management, drinking water and wastewater emergencies, environmental sampling) with tempo-appropriate decision making and documentation. Observable: incident action plan inputs, position task book completion, after-action reports.
rationale: v1 ICS exists only for wildland fire; environmental emergency response is a core EPA/state function.

proposed_title: Administer floodplain management regulations and the NFIP locally
description: Reviews development permits against floodplain ordinances, makes substantial-damage/improvement determinations, manages elevation certificates and map changes, and runs Community Rating System activities. Observable: permit decisions, SD/SI determinations, CRS documentation.
rationale: Local floodplain administrator is a common, credentialed (CFM) role absent in v1.

proposed_title: Prepare assurance-ready sustainability disclosures across reporting regimes
description: Maps disclosure obligations across jurisdictions and standards (ISSB/IFRS S1-S2, ESRS, California climate laws, voluntary frameworks), designs internal controls over sustainability data, and supports limited/reasonable assurance. Observable: disclosure with control documentation and assurance findings resolved.
rationale: Replaces v1 3.6.2 tasks citing the abandoned SEC rule and blockchain; the durable competency is regime-agnostic, controls-based disclosure.

proposed_title: Manage supply-chain environmental data and due diligence
description: Engages suppliers for emissions and environmental data, estimates Scope 3 and product footprints with stated uncertainty, and conducts due diligence for regulated commodities (e.g., deforestation-free requirements). Observable: supplier data program, footprint with uncertainty, due-diligence statements.
rationale: Main growth area of corporate sustainability work [J].

proposed_title: Assess the integrity of environmental credits and offsets
description: Evaluates credits against integrity criteria (additionality, baseline, leakage, permanence, MRV quality, double counting, safeguards) using standards such as the ICVCM CCPs; documents risk ratings and purchase or approval decisions. Observable: integrity assessment with evidence trail.
rationale: v1 markets competencies describe transactions but not integrity judgment, the main skill gap after credit-quality scandals [J].

proposed_title: Administer compensatory mitigation programs
description: Reviews and approves bank, in-lieu fee and permittee-responsible mitigation (credit-debit methods, performance standards, financial assurances, long-term management) as an IRT member, sponsor or reviewer. Observable: mitigation plan review, credit ledger decisions, compliance monitoring.
rationale: v1 6.6.2 frames biodiversity credits as trading; regulatory mitigation administration is the larger public function.

proposed_title: Implement coastal zone management and shoreline permitting
description: Applies state coastal program policies and CZMA federal consistency, reviews shoreline and coastal development, promotes living shorelines and plans for sea-level rise. Observable: consistency determinations, permit decisions, SLR adaptation plans.
rationale: v1 itself flagged marine/coastal as a missing family.

proposed_title: Conduct fisheries stock assessment and develop management advice
description: Integrates catch, survey, observer/electronic-monitoring and biological data into stock assessment models (including data-limited methods), characterizes uncertainty and advises managers on catch limits. Observable: assessment report, peer-review responses, management advice.
rationale: v1 population dynamics is generic; stock assessment is a distinct federal/state scientific product.

proposed_title: Conduct Section 106 and state historic preservation review and consultation
description: Defines the area of potential effects, identifies and evaluates historic properties (NRHP criteria), assesses effects, and consults with SHPOs, THPOs, Tribes and others to agreement documents. Observable: identification report, effect finding, executed MOA/PA.
rationale: v1 5.3.3 covers identification only; cultural terms appear in 835 forest-plan components [E: DB-011]. TN must govern Tribal-knowledge aspects.

proposed_title: Integrate environmental commitments into transportation project delivery
description: Carries environmental review commitments from NEPA/Section 4(f)/permits through design, construction and maintenance using commitment tracking; manages NEPA assignment responsibilities where applicable. Observable: commitment register, construction compliance records.
rationale: State DOTs are among the largest employers of NEPA practitioners [J]; v1 has no transport-specific competency.

proposed_title: Conduct cumulative impact analysis for permitting decisions
description: Assembles stressor and population data, applies a defined cumulative-impact method, engages affected communities, and translates results into permit decisions or conditions as required by state law. Observable: cumulative impact assessment and resulting permit conditions.
rationale: State cumulative-impact laws (e.g., New Jersey) create a regulatory product beyond screening.

proposed_title: Generate legally defensible environmental analytical data
description: Selects approved methods, maintains QA/QC (calibration, blanks, spikes, detection limits), documents chain of custody, and validates data for usability in regulatory decisions. Observable: QA records, data validation reports, proficiency test results.
rationale: Labs produce the evidence base for compliance; absent in v1.

proposed_title: Monitor conservation easements and enforce their terms
description: Prepares baseline documentation, conducts monitoring (field and remote sensing), documents violations and negotiates resolution or enforcement. Observable: baseline report, monitoring records, resolved violations.
rationale: Land trust stewardship core task; absent in v1.

proposed_title: Manage grazing permits and allotments
description: Administers grazing authorizations, sets and adjusts stocking and seasons using monitoring, coordinates range improvements and permittee relations, and documents decisions. Observable: allotment management plan, annual operating instructions, monitoring-based adjustments.
rationale: Grazing/allotment terms in 2,709 forest-plan components [E: DB-011]; v1 lacks the administrative competency.

proposed_title: Conduct interagency consultation on listed species and prepare biological assessments
description: Determine effects of a proposed action on listed species and critical habitat, prepare biological assessments, and negotiate conservation measures through formal and informal consultation.
rationale: Recurring grade-relevant duty in 0486/0482/0401 positions at FWS, NOAA and action agencies; v1 6.1.2 is too generic to anchor SME-QA benchmarks. Coordinate wording with SC (statute-neutral core plus federal enactment note).

proposed_title: Prepare and administer timber sale, stewardship and partner implementation agreements
description: Translate silvicultural or restoration prescriptions into sale layouts, appraisals, contract/agreement specifications and inspections, and enforce compliance through the contract term.
rationale: Grade-controlling duty in 0460 PDs (v1 illustrative PD 20%) missing from F1 Core; growing as agencies rely on partners after 2025 cuts.

proposed_title: Develop conservation plans with private landowners and deliver voluntary conservation programs
description: Inventory resource concerns with producers, evaluate alternatives against practice standards, and write, contract and verify conservation plans and program payments.
rationale: Core NRCS 0457/0458 work (Farm Bill delivery) with no v1 home; also the main federal-to-conservation-district mobility bridge.

proposed_title: Administer grazing permits and monitor allotment conditions
description: Evaluate rangeland condition and utilization against allotment objectives, adjust terms and conditions, document NEPA for renewals, and resolve permittee non-compliance.
rationale: Grade-controlling for BLM/USFS 0454; v1 5.5.2 is a customer-service frame.

proposed_title: Calibrate remote-sensing and AI-derived resource inventories against field measurements
description: Design ground-truth sampling, quantify error and bias in LiDAR/imagery/model products for local conditions, and decide where field plots remain necessary.
rationale: From v1 forester PD redesign; generalizes across inventory series (0460, 0454, 0408, 0470). Overlaps DC lane - DC to own wording.

proposed_title: Design structured developmental field experiences for entry-level staff
description: Plan task-book, rotation and mentored field assignments that build judgment once automated tools absorb traditional entry tasks; document sign-off evidence.
rationale: Entry pipeline contracted in 2025 (student-trainee occupations down; under-30 share 7.9%); v1 CLD flags show where entry tasks compress. LC/FC lanes for content; FH for supervisory duty language.

proposed_title: Capture and transfer critical institutional and place-based knowledge before staff separate
description: Identify single-incumbent knowledge, elicit it through structured interviews, shadowing and annotated records, and verify that successors can apply it.
rationale: ~317,000 departures in 2025 (DRP ~144k) and 35.7% -> ~40% aged 50+ make knowledge transfer a workforce-planning necessity; v1 2.5.4 is a tool frame.

proposed_title: Conduct cultural resource compliance reviews for federal undertakings
description: Identify historic properties, assess effects, consult with SHPO/THPO and Tribes, and document resolution of adverse effects.
rationale: Statutory gate on most land-management projects (0193/0170 series); v1 5.3.3 covers identification only. TN must review Tribal-facing wording.

proposed_title: Maintain incident qualifications and serve in incident roles as a collateral duty
description: Hold and maintain interagency incident qualifications, complete position task books, and perform assigned incident roles alongside a primary non-fire job.
rationale: USFS reports ~10,000 non-fire staff with fire qualifications; ~1,600 fire-certified staff left by May 2025. The 'militia' is a distinct, shrinking capability that role profiles must show.

proposed_title: Operate fish hatchery and aquatic propagation programs
description: Manage broodstock, genetics, fish health, rearing and release to meet recovery or harvest objectives.
rationale: FWS/NOAA/tribal hatcheries employ 0482 and technicians; no v1 home.

proposed_title: Conduct environmental compliance inspections and develop enforcement cases
description: Plan and perform facility inspections, collect admissible evidence, evaluate violations, and prepare case referrals.
rationale: Rewrite of 6.1.5 for 0028/1801 and state inspectors; remote sensing and AI targeting are changing inspection selection.

proposed_title: Oversee investigation and cleanup of contaminated sites
description: Scope site characterization, evaluate remedial alternatives, oversee remedial contractors, and verify cleanup performance.
rationale: Major 0819/0028/1301 workload (EPA, DoD, DOE) with no v1 home; DB to place in a remediation module.

proposed_title: Write job analyses, crediting plans and assessment benchmarks for technical positions
description: Translate position duties into task and competency ratings, proficiency benchmarks and structured-interview questions with SMEs, and document job-relatedness.
rationale: Chance to Compete makes SMEs co-authors of hiring; FY25 91% of DE announcements relied only on self-report questionnaires and only 15% of agencies employ I-O psychologists. Supervisors and senior specialists need this as a competency (IO lane for method).

proposed_title: Justify positions and staffing with workload and mission evidence
description: Quantify workload, statutory requirements and risk to support position requests before hiring committees and in annual staffing plans.
rationale: EO 14356 requires Strategic Hiring Committee approval of each vacancy and annual staffing plans; supervisors who can evidence need get positions filled.

proposed_title: Use AI drafting tools for environmental documents with documented human review
description: Apply agency-approved AI tools to draft, summarize or review environmental analyses and decision documents, verify content against source records, and keep auditable records of review.
rationale: OPM now treats AI-assisted drafting as acceptable when documented and human-adopted; the same standard is becoming the expectation for program documents. Coordinate with DC (transversal vs datacraft).

proposed_title: Deploy, maintain and verify field sensor networks
description: Site, install, power, secure, service and verify autonomous field instruments (acoustic recorders, camera traps, water-quality sondes, weather and soil stations, low-cost air sensors) so that continuous data streams stay valid; diagnose drift, fouling, damage and siting bias in place.
subsector: cross-cutting monitoring (wildlife, water, air, forestry, agriculture)
rationale: Continuous monitoring moves field work from observing to instrument stewardship; the defining deliverable (valid data at the point of measurement) fails in the field and is caught in the field. v1 tags this DC-primary.

proposed_title: Ground-truth remote, modeled and AI-generated outputs in the field
description: Plan and collect field reference data to test maps, model outputs and automated classifications (burn severity, canopy/fuels, habitat, land cover, mortality, detections); record disagreement and its causes; feed corrections back to analysts.
rationale: Every scaled remote product needs a field reference; v1 lists ground-truthing only as FC-secondary inside DC competencies, so the field half of validation has no home and no proficiency scale.

proposed_title: Adjudicate automated species detections using field-formed identification expertise
description: Review AI-suggested identifications from images, audio and eDNA hits; confirm, reject or escalate; recognize look-alikes, regional and seasonal implausibility; target field confirmation where needed; document decisions for model retraining.
rationale: Often done on a screen, but the expertise is formed in the field. Tagging it DC would hide the field formation that makes it work (formation_dependency=yes). Expected point of disagreement with DC.

proposed_title: Conduct on-site environmental compliance inspections
description: Plan and carry out inspections of facilities, sites and practices (air, water, waste, stormwater/BMPs, grazing, timber, reclamation, permit conditions); recognize violations and risk from site conditions; collect defensible evidence (photos, samples, measurements, notes); communicate with regulated parties on site.
subsector: compliance and enforcement (air, water, waste, land use)
rationale: A large, mostly state and local field workforce that v1 cannot see (6.1.2 T1 field inspections sits inside an SC competency with no FC tag). Integration point: observation and evidence are FC; legal authority and compliance negotiation are SC.

proposed_title: Conduct field investigations at contaminated sites
description: Execute site characterization and remediation-support field work: soil, groundwater and soil-gas sampling; field screening instruments; well installation oversight; PPE level selection; decontamination; health and safety plan compliance; chain of custody.
rationale: Missing subsector field craft (consulting and state cleanup programs are major employers). v1 4.4.4 treats hazmat only as an emergency.

proposed_title: Delineate wetlands and other aquatic resources
description: Determine wetland boundaries using vegetation, hydric soil and hydrology indicators under the federal manual and regional supplements; complete data forms; map boundaries; support jurisdictional determinations and permit applications.
rationale: No wetland competency exists in v1. Jurisdiction changes do not remove the field determination; remote wetland mapping raises the need for field verification.

proposed_title: Assess stream channel form and function in the field
description: Measure and interpret channel geometry, substrate, bankfull indicators, habitat units and riparian condition; recognize channel evolution stage and process drivers; use results to design and monitor restoration.
rationale: No geomorphic field assessment competency in v1; it underpins restoration design and post-flood response.

proposed_title: Monitor rangeland condition with calibrated field indicators
description: Apply standardized core indicators (e.g., line-point intercept, canopy gap, soil stability) and qualitative rangeland health assessment; calibrate with other observers; integrate with remote-sensing cover products and permittee knowledge.
rationale: Rangeland monitoring is absent from v1 except via grazing mentions; large federal programs depend on seasonal field crews.

proposed_title: Manage vegetation near utility infrastructure
description: Inspect and prioritize vegetation risk near lines and assets; verify remote-sensing risk scores in the field; direct pruning and removal under line-clearance safety rules; work with landowners on rights-of-way.
rationale: One of the largest private-sector field vegetation workforces, driven by wildfire mitigation; absent from v1.

proposed_title: Detect and rapidly respond to invasive species
description: Plan and run early-detection surveys at high-risk pathways; confirm detections (including eDNA and AI detections) in the field; implement rapid containment; coordinate notification.
rationale: v1 4.2.2 covers control only; early detection and rapid response is a distinct, time-critical field capacity.

proposed_title: Apply field biosecurity and decontamination protocols
description: Prevent movement of pathogens and invasive organisms on gear, boats, vehicles and people (e.g., aquatic invasives, amphibian chytrid, white-nose syndrome, plant pathogens); select and verify decontamination methods; train crews.
rationale: No biosecurity content in v1 despite being routine field practice; failures are irreversible.

proposed_title: Operate small boats and conduct aquatic, marine and coastal field work safely
description: Operate motorboats and small vessels; plan around tides, currents, weather and cold water; deploy and recover sampling gear from vessels; manage vessel emergencies.
rationale: No marine/coastal or vessel content in v1; a coverage gap beyond public lands (DB should extend).

proposed_title: Conduct cultural resource field survey and monitoring
description: Perform pedestrian survey, shovel testing and site recording under applicable standards; apply inadvertent-discovery protocols; work alongside Tribal monitors on their terms. Co-draft with TN; Tribal knowledge content is not codified here.
rationale: v1 5.3.3 has no proficiency content. Field survey craft is distinct from Section 106 process (SC). TN decides any Tribal-knowledge dimension.

proposed_title: Operate and supervise uncrewed and automated field systems
description: Plan, launch, supervise and recover uncrewed aircraft, vessels and ground systems (including beyond-visual-line-of-sight and multi-aircraft operations and UAS aerial ignition); coordinate airspace and crews; intervene when automation fails; maintain airworthiness and data integrity.
rationale: Replaces tool-bound 4.5.4/2.3.2/4.6.2. USFS flew ~4,500 UAS hours in FY24 with 99% collateral-duty pilots; Part 108 shifts accountability to organizations and introduces supervisory roles over multiple aircraft.

proposed_title: Capture, handle and mark wildlife and fish humanely and safely
description: Plan and conduct live capture (traps, nets, electrofishing, chemical immobilization where authorized), handling, marking and tagging; minimize stress and injury; manage zoonotic and personal safety risks; follow animal-care protocols.
rationale: Core wildlife/fisheries field skill missing as a competency; telemetry and biologging increase rather than remove capture work.

proposed_title: Collect environmental samples for trace, emerging-contaminant and genetic analysis without contamination
description: Apply clean sampling methods for trace metals, PFAS and eDNA; choose sites, timing and replication for detection; run field blanks; prevent cross-contamination; preserve and ship samples within holding times.
subsector: water, soil and air quality; biodiversity
rationale: Lower detection limits make field contamination the dominant error source; durable competency behind method-specific v1 1.6.2.

proposed_title: Operate and audit ambient air monitoring stations and sensors
description: Operate, calibrate and audit regulatory monitors and low-cost sensors; site and colocate sensors; handle filters and samples; document station conditions; support community monitoring networks.
rationale: v1 classifies air monitoring as dashboard supervision (6.7.5 T1 V/Lo); the networks depend on field operators.

proposed_title: Navigate and work safely in remote terrain with and without digital aids
description: Plan routes; navigate by map, compass and GPS; recognize and recover from GPS or device failure; manage check-in and lone-worker systems; assess terrain, weather and water-crossing hazards.
rationale: v1 flagged GPS dependence as a Delphi question (4.4.3 T2) but has no durable navigation competency; recast from SAR.

proposed_title: Prevent and manage heat, smoke and environmental exposure illness in field crews
description: Plan work-rest, hydration and acclimatization; monitor heat and smoke exposure; recognize early illness; adapt schedules and stop work; meet applicable rules.
rationale: Rising heat exposure and a pending federal heat standard (status unverified) make this a growing field competency; currently buried in generic safety.

proposed_title: Lead field crews and transfer field judgment to novices
description: Lead small crews in the field; make field cues explicit to novices; design graduated exposure; run tailgate briefings and after-action reviews; decide when a novice is ready for independent work.
rationale: With smaller crews and fewer seasonal hires, deliberate transfer of tacit field judgment becomes a named competency. 7.2.2 designs the system; this is doing it in the field.

proposed_title: Work alongside landowners, permittees, volunteers and communities on the land
description: Conduct joint field visits; read the site together with landowners, permittees, ranchers, foresters and volunteers; reconcile local observations with protocol data; explain field findings and their limits face to face.
rationale: Working with people on the land is a field component v1 assigns wholly to SC. Integration point with SC: institutional authority stays SC; shared field reading is FC.

proposed_title: Read site history and reference conditions from landscape evidence
description: Interpret land-use legacies, disturbance history and reference conditions from field evidence (fire scars, stumps, soil horizons, legacy structures, vegetation patterns) and reconcile with records and local knowledge holders who choose to share.
rationale: Place knowledge and temporal depth have no explicit competency in v1; they drive restoration and novel-ecosystem calls.

proposed_title: Record field observations with protocol fidelity and data integrity
description: Record complete, accurate and well-documented observations in any medium; apply protocol rules and metadata under adverse conditions; flag conditions that compromise data; recover from device failure.
rationale: Durable rewrite of tool-bound 4.1.5; app skills move to the tool layer.

proposed_title: Manage field sample custody and field quality control
description: Plan and document field QC (blanks, duplicates, splits, instrument calibration logs), chain of custody and holding times; recognize and report field conditions that invalidate samples.
rationale: No chain-of-custody or field QC content anywhere in v1; this is what makes field data legally and scientifically defensible.

proposed_title: Conduct rapid post-disaster field assessments
description: Assess burned, flooded, storm-damaged or landslide-affected sites rapidly; verify remote damage maps; identify immediate hazards (falling trees, debris flows, contamination); prioritize stabilization.
rationale: Generalizes the BAER pattern beyond fire as climate disasters grow.

proposed_title: Assess tree risk and structural condition
description: Evaluate tree defects, failure likelihood and targets using standard methods and diagnostic tools; recommend mitigation; document for liability.
rationale: Missing; central to urban forestry, utilities and hazard-tree work on public lands.

proposed_title: Manage risk where people work alongside automated field systems
description: Identify and control hazards from drones near crewed aircraft and crews, autonomous or teleoperated machines, lithium battery fires, and automation-induced complacency; set stop-work criteria; integrate into job hazard analysis.
rationale: Technology moves risk rather than removing it (GAO: grounding drones shifted aerial ignition back to helicopters, which officials said raises personnel risk).

proposed_title: Plan and run field campaigns and remote logistics
description: Plan field seasons and campaigns: access permissions, scheduling against phenology and weather windows, equipment readiness, remote camps, resupply, communications and contingency plans.
rationale: Unnamed in v1 but determines whether field programs deliver; increasingly falls on fewer, more senior staff.

proposed_title: Measure and verify carbon and ecosystem-service field plots
description: Install and measure carbon and ecosystem-service plots to protocol; conduct verification site visits; reconcile field measurements with remote-sensing estimates; document for registries.
rationale: v1 rates the measurement task Ac/Lo; field verification is high-tacit and its future depends on remote MRV adoption (PS and LM to supply evidence).

proposed_title: Implement process-based and low-tech restoration
description: Design and build low-tech structures (e.g., beaver dam analogues, post-assisted log structures) and process-based treatments; read site response and adapt.
rationale: A fast-spreading field practice that relies on reading channel and floodplain response rather than engineered design.

proposed_title: Calibrate observers and run field measurement quality assurance
description: Run observer calibration, hot/cold/blind check re-measurements and field audits; compute and interpret agreement against tolerances; retrain or re-assign observers.
rationale: The mechanism by which field programs make proficiency observable; also the basis for assessment anchors.

proposed_title: Evaluate and certify others' task performance against position standards
description: Observes trainees or staff performing position tasks, rates performance against written standards using an entrustment-supervision scale, gives corrective feedback, and documents qualification or entrustment decisions that a second evaluator would reproduce.
subsector: cross-cutting (wildland fire, field monitoring, inspection, laboratory, operations)
rationale: v1 covers supervision (3.3.1) and the design of formation workflows (7.2.2), but has no competency for the act of assessing another person's performance to a standard. Task-book and entrustment systems, which v2 relies on for training-use validity (validation_protocol.md s.8.2), stand or fall on evaluator quality. Contraction and AI compression of entry-level tasks make deliberate, well-evaluated practice more important. Assessable: inter-evaluator agreement on observed trainees; quality of documented decisions.

proposed_title: Serve as a subject-matter expert in merit-based hiring assessments
description: Contributes technical expertise to job analysis; writes and reviews job-related assessment content (structured-interview questions with behavioral anchors, work samples, résumé-review criteria); and rates applicants consistently against defined criteria within merit-system and anti-discrimination rules.
rationale: Federal skills-based hiring (SME-QA; Chance to Compete Act technical assessments; Merit Hiring Plan) puts line practitioners into job analysis and applicant rating. Their rating consistency directly affects the legality and quality of hires. v1 has no such competency. Assessable: rater-calibration exercises against expert-keyed ratings; quality review of written interview questions and anchors. Evidence label E-u: the policy sources were not re-retrieved this session.

proposed_title: Elicit and document tacit expertise from experienced practitioners
description: Plans and conducts structured knowledge-elicitation sessions (critical-decision interviews, field walk-throughs, after-action reviews) with experienced practitioners, and converts the results into documented cues, decision rules and training cases that others can use and verify.
rationale: v1 Scenarios C and D (Structural Conditions report) warn of irreversible tacit-knowledge loss as experienced cohorts leave and entry cohorts shrink. Elicitation is a teachable method (critical-incident and cognitive task analysis) with assessable outputs (documented cues and decision rules validated by a second expert). The same skill supplies the critical incidents that v2 BARS development needs. LC overlap: knowledge capture for curriculum.

proposed_title: Design and run plan-level monitoring programs that answer management questions
description: Translate plan components into monitoring questions and indicators, select methods and data sources, run evaluation cycles and report results that trigger management responses
rationale: 2012-rule plans: 22% of components are monitoring; 1,506 explicit monitoring questions; v1 covers performance monitoring and adaptive management generically but not plan monitoring programs

proposed_title: Manage recreation settings and visitor use to sustain resources and experiences
description: Apply recreation opportunity and scenery classifications, estimate visitor use and capacity, manage travel and access, and monitor social and resource conditions
rationale: Recreation is the largest theme in standards (15%) and monitoring questions (17%); ROS in 62 plans, scenery classes in 68; v1 has only visitor information services. Flag to DB/FC for drafting

proposed_title: Administer resource-use authorizations (grazing, minerals, special uses) and their compliance
description: Process, condition, monitor and enforce authorizations for grazing, mineral activity and special uses, coordinating required consultations
rationale: Plan components mention grazing in 1,785, mining in 1,075 and special uses in 924; authorization touchpoints total 796; v1 5.5.2 is generic permit administration. Overlaps SC lane

proposed_title: Steward and interpret the authoritative datasets and models behind plan requirements
description: Maintain, quality-check and analyse agency corporate data and reference models (inventory, vegetation maps, range-of-variation analyses, watershed condition, fire regime, visitor monitoring) and explain their limits in decisions
rationale: Plans depend on agency classifications and corporate systems (ROS 62 plans; hydrologic models 53; NRV 37; corporate systems 28; FIA 18; LANDFIRE 14) more than on named AI tools; durable data-stewardship competence, tool names belong in L4

proposed_title: Sustain institutional knowledge through workforce attrition and succession
description: Identify critical tacit knowledge held by departing staff, design capture and transfer (paired work, after-action records, mentoring), and rebuild review capacity when senior reviewers leave
rationale: EPA departing staff median tenure ~30 years; USFS/NPS losses >16-25%; v1 7.2.2 addresses tacit formation under AI but not knowledge loss under attrition - the binding constraint in 2025-26

proposed_title: Use labor-market and AI-change evidence in workforce and training plans
description: Read exposure indices, usage data, posting and headcount signals with their limits; set staffing and training priorities; avoid treating exposure scores as job-loss forecasts
rationale: EO 14356 annual staffing plans and AI strategies require managers to justify positions; no v1 competency covers evidence-based workforce planning for program managers (borderline; IO/FH to judge whether it belongs in a manager role profile)

proposed_title: Design and run performance-based qualification for field and technical work
description: Define observable task standards, build task-book style performance records, train and calibrate evaluators, code evaluations by context (field, incident, desk, public setting), and maintain currency rules.
rationale: Performance evidence is the only defensible route to credit field and statecraft competence; v1 has no competency for the people who run it, and staffing losses make evaluator capacity a bottleneck.

proposed_title: Mentor and assess practitioners on the job to transmit tacit field and institutional knowledge
description: Plan supervised repetitions, narrate judgment in context, give structured feedback, and record what was observed so formation survives turnover and AI-assisted workflows.
rationale: CLD signals mean entry tasks that used to form judgment are being compressed; formation must be designed and someone must be competent to do it. Indicators mention mentoring 43 times but no competency owns it.

proposed_title: Identify regionally important plant and tree species using diagnostic features and keys
description: Identify species, genus and family from leaves, twigs, bark, fruit and form; use dichotomous keys; know distribution and associated biota.
rationale: Required by SAF Forestry and Forest Technology standards; absent from v1 (1.4.3 covers animals only). Also the field skill that AI plant-ID apps tempt learners to skip, which makes it a validation baseline.

proposed_title: Ground-truth and calibrate remote-sensing and AI products with field measurements
description: Design calibration plots, compare model or imagery outputs with field measurements, quantify error, and feed corrections back to analysts and models.
rationale: The career bridge from field technician to remote-sensing analyst (LC-PW-03). It sits between 1.3.2, 2.1.2 T3 and 7.2.1; DC/FC should decide whether it is new or a rewrite of 2.1.2 T3.

proposed_title: Operate and optimize water and wastewater treatment processes using real-time sensor and control-system data
description: Run treatment unit processes to permit limits, interpret online analyzer and control-system trends, distinguish sensor drift from process change, and act on alarms.
rationale: Large public workforce with registered apprenticeships and state certification but no v1 home; required for pathway LC-PW-05. DB should own module content.

proposed_title: Apply operational-technology cybersecurity practices to environmental monitoring and utility systems
description: Recognize and report OT security risks, follow access and patching procedures for sensors and control systems, and keep manual fallback operations ready.
rationale: Sensor-based monitoring expands the attack surface; no source on environmental OT cybersecurity was read this session, so this is a placeholder for DC/DB to evidence or drop.

proposed_title: Investigate and control environmental public health hazards in food, vectors and zoonotic disease
description: Conduct inspections and investigations, apply epidemiological reasoning to outbreaks and exposures, and select control measures.
rationale: EHAC List 1 requires these areas; county and state environmental health is a major employer absent from v1. DB to scope as an environmental-health module.

proposed_title: Transfer place-based and institutional knowledge through structured handover
description: Plans and runs handovers when staff leave or when work moves between sector actors: identifies critical tacit knowledge (sites, relationships, decision history, local protocols), captures it with the departing holder, and confirms the receiving team can act on it
rationale: Evidenced need: work is devolving between actors and named tacit skills were lost in one season. v1 has records management (3.3.5) and tacit-formation design (7.2.2) but no competency for knowledge continuity across institutional handoffs. Tribal knowledge is out of scope unless holders choose (TN)

proposed_title: Translate competencies and experience across sector-actor hiring systems
description: Expresses one's own or a candidate's competencies in the terms a different sector actor's hiring system credits (class specs, qualification standards, private job architectures), with evidence that an assessor will accept
rationale: Practitioners report that people must learn to articulate skills in employers' terms, and badges confuse employers. A teachable career-practice capability for workers, HR intermediaries and corps staff. LC and IO to decide whether it belongs in the transversal layer or in learning-path design only

proposed_title: Work within cross-actor co-delivery agreements
