description: Plans, staffs and delivers environmental work under agreements that cross sector-actor lines (e.g. Good Neighbor agreements, shared stewardship, special use permits to counties), including shared accountability, data exchange and staff exchange (e.g. IPA assignments)
rationale: Devolution of federal functions creates demand for this capability. v1 6.5.2 (federal-state-local coordination) covers coordination, not delivery under agreement. Offered to SC for decision; SC owns statecraft content

proposed_title: Manage client relationships and scope for environmental services
description: Define client needs, negotiate scope, assumptions and exclusions, manage expectations and scope changes (change orders) for environmental studies, permits and compliance services; mirrors the COR/program-officer role on the public side.
rationale: Universal private hiring criterion for mid-level consulting roles; absent from v1 (only 38 of 222 Consulting notes mention clients). Observable via scope documents and change-order logs.

proposed_title: Develop business and write winning proposals for environmental work
description: Make go/no-go decisions, build capture plans, write technical approaches, assemble past performance and price work for RFPs, task orders and grants; transfers to NGO and public grant-seeking.
rationale: The seller-doer expectation is the main private career accelerator and has no v1 home; proposal writing is also the NGO and Tribal funding bottleneck. Assess via proposal samples and win/loss records.

proposed_title: Deliver billable environmental projects to budget, schedule and quality
description: Plan and track labor hours against budget (estimate-at-completion), utilization and margin; manage subcontractors; run QA/QC review before deliverables; invoice to contract terms.
rationale: v1 3.1 is generic project management; billable delivery has distinct, observable metrics. AI compresses hours and pressures time-and-materials billing, so this competency is changing now.

proposed_title: Assess regulatory and permitting risk for transactions and investment
description: Evaluate how permits, liabilities, litigation and regulatory change affect a project's schedule, cost and value for owners, lenders and investors; express findings as investor-grade risk opinions.
rationale: Rising demand as permitting reform and disclosure regimes shift (SEC rescission, CA in force); bridges regulators to investors. No v1 competency frames regulation as a financial risk.

proposed_title: Prepare sustainability information for external assurance
description: Design and document internal controls, evidence trails and calculation methods so GHG and sustainability disclosures withstand limited and later reasonable assurance; manage assurance-provider requests.
rationale: California requires limited assurance from 2026 and reasonable from 2030 (PS-001, PS-003); EU dropped reasonable assurance (PS-005); ESG-controller roles emerging (PS-012). v1 3.6.2 has no controls/assurance content.

proposed_title: Operate and validate digital MRV for carbon and nature outcomes
description: Combine remote sensing, models and field plots to quantify carbon or habitat outcomes; quantify uncertainty; design ground-truth sampling that satisfies registry and verifier requirements.
rationale: dMRV firms and raters hire on this; v1 splits pieces across 2.x and 6.6.1 with no integrity framing. Durable core is uncertainty and validation, not specific platforms.

proposed_title: Verify greenhouse gas assertions and environmental claims independently
description: Plan and conduct validation/verification of GHG inventories, offset projects and environmental claims to recognized standards, including site visits, sampling, materiality thresholds and independence safeguards.
rationale: Verification bodies and assurance firms hire on this; CARB lists independence and no-self-review as provider attributes (PS-003). Distinct from preparing an inventory.

proposed_title: Apply carbon-credit integrity criteria to projects and portfolios
description: Assess additionality, baselines, leakage, permanence and reversal risk, co-benefits and safeguards against integrity frameworks when developing, rating or buying credits.
rationale: Replaces three overlapping v1 competencies (6.3.5, 6.6.3, 6.8.3) with one observable integrity competency; raters, buyers and developers all hire on it.

proposed_title: Build corporate greenhouse gas inventories across Scopes 1-3 for multiple disclosure regimes
description: Set organizational and operational boundaries, select emission factors and estimation methods, compile Scope 3 categories and map one inventory to ISSB, ESRS and California requirements.
rationale: Split corporate inventories from project quantification in 6.6.1. Multi-regime reconciliation is the 2026 skill (PS-008); reported 12-18% premium (PS-013, low quality).

proposed_title: Run environmental compliance through a management system
description: Maintain permit-condition registers and compliance calendars, assign accountabilities, run internal audits and corrective action, and support certifying officials, using an ISO 14001-type management system.
rationale: Core of every in-house EHS job; v1 6.1.2 is assessment-only. Public facilities (bases, labs, utilities) need the same competency, so it also supports mobility.

proposed_title: Lead applicant-side permitting strategy for infrastructure projects
description: Sequence federal, state and local permits on the project critical path, choose consultants, negotiate with agencies, and manage permitting risk and community commitments.
rationale: v1 6.1.3 mixes agency-side review and applicant-side strategy; the applicant side is a distinct, high-demand private role (developers, utilities).

proposed_title: Plan and manage utility vegetation and wildfire mitigation programs
description: Design risk-based vegetation cycles and wildfire mitigation activities to regulatory and reliability standards; manage contractor workforces; report to regulators.
rationale: Large and growing private field-craft employer with no v1 home. Coordinate with DB (energy/utilities coverage) and FC.

proposed_title: Conduct environmental due diligence for property transactions
description: Perform records review, site reconnaissance, interviews and recognized-environmental-condition judgments meeting federal all-appropriate-inquiries rules; scope Phase II sampling.
rationale: High-volume entry-level consulting work; records-review portion is highly AI-compressible while the site visit and environmental-professional judgment are not.

proposed_title: Manage compensatory mitigation and habitat-bank credit lifecycles
description: Establish banks or in-lieu fee programs, prepare instruments, meet performance standards for credit release, and plan long-term management and financial assurance.
rationale: Rewrite of 6.6.2: the mature US wetland/species banking market is the real private demand; biodiversity credits are the emerging extension.

proposed_title: Negotiate land rights and rights-of-way for environmental and infrastructure projects
description: Acquire leases, options and easements; resolve title; manage landowner relationships and compensation; align with permitting and conservation commitments.
rationale: Missing from v1; public realty specialists (1170) and private land agents share it, so it is a strong mobility bridge.

proposed_title: Engage suppliers and growers to reduce supply-chain environmental impacts
description: Design and run supplier and grower programs (practice payments, data collection, verification) that reduce Scope 3 and sourcing impacts while sustaining supplier relationships.
rationale: Sourcing-sustainability roles at food and ag firms hire on this; v1 has agronomy and corporate engagement but not the supply-chain bridge.

proposed_title: Comply with producer-responsibility and product environmental regulations
description: Track and meet packaging EPR, chemical (including PFAS) reporting and product-claim rules across jurisdictions; maintain product data and filings.
rationale: Growing state-law-driven compliance roles; v1 3.7 is framed as voluntary circular strategy. Coordinate with DB (waste and circular economy).

proposed_title: Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary
description: Recognize and disclose conflicts when preparing documents for regulatory decisions, verifying claims, or moving between agency and private roles; apply revolving-door and independence rules.
rationale: Extends 7.1.3 to applicant-prepared documents, third-party verification and staff moving between sectors. Mobility increases the need for it.

proposed_title: Price and disclose AI-augmented environmental services
description: Estimate effort and price work when AI changes labor hours; choose fixed-fee or value pricing; disclose AI use and validation steps to clients and regulators.
rationale: Speculative but plausible: hour-based billing does not survive large drafting compression. Confirm via firm disclosures, procurement policies and contract-clause changes.

proposed_title: Certify AI-drafted regulatory and technical deliverables under professional liability
description: Review, verify and accept responsibility for AI-generated drafts of permits, reports and analyses before signing or stamping; document what was checked and how.
rationale: Specializes 7.2.1 to the stamp/signatory point (PE, PG, Environmental Professional, responsible official), where private liability concentrates.

proposed_title: Analyze climate-related physical and transition risk for financial disclosure
description: Run scenario analysis and translate hazard and transition data into financially material risks and opportunities under IFRS S2-aligned requirements.
rationale: Rewrite of 6.8.5: TCFD is folded into ISSB; SB 261 enjoined; more than 45 jurisdictions on the ISSB path.

proposed_title: Assess and disclose nature-related dependencies, impacts and risks
description: Screen sites and value chains for nature dependencies and impacts, prioritize locations and prepare nature-related disclosures and targets.
rationale: ISSB nature-related draft expected by Oct 2026 (PS-008). A natural landing place for ecologists moving into private roles.

proposed_title: Manage forests to certification-scheme standards
description: Implement and evidence conformance with SFI, FSC or PEFC forest-management and fiber-sourcing standards; prepare for and respond to audits.
rationale: Timberland employers and auditors hire on this; absent from v1.

proposed_title: Work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized sites
description: Apply HAZWOPER, site health-and-safety plans, confined-space and electrical line-clearance rules when conducting field work at contaminated, industrial or utility sites.
rationale: HAZWOPER is the de facto entry gate for consulting field staff; v1 4.4.4 is awareness-level and wilderness-oriented.

proposed_title: Administer a delegated or primacy environmental program
description: Run a state-, Tribal- or locally-administered program under federal authorization: maintain program authority, meet federal oversight and reporting obligations, write grant work plans, and keep state rules at least as stringent as federal minimums.
rationale: Most state environmental work is delegated or primacy program administration, which v1 never names (0 mentions of primacy or delegation in v1 text). v1 6.5.2 treats coordination as a relationship skill, not as administering a program under another government's oversight.

proposed_title: Write and issue environmental permits as the regulatory authority
description: Derive permit limits and conditions from statute, rules and technical analysis (e.g. NPDES effluent limits linked to TMDLs); draft fact sheets and deficiency letters; respond to comments; issue or deny; defend the record.
rationale: v1 6.1.3 and stage S3 are written from the applicant side ('securing regulatory authorization'). State postings describe the permit-writer side, a different task bundle with different AI exposure (drafting is compressible; limit derivation and defensibility are not).

proposed_title: Conduct regulatory compliance inspections
description: Plan and conduct facility or site inspections against permit conditions and rules; collect evidence and samples to evidentiary standard; document findings; issue notices of violation or compliance assistance.
rationale: Inspection is the modal state and local environmental task (TX EPS and NRS, PA EPS, FL DEP). v1 6.1.2 'Regulatory compliance assessment' merges inspector and regulated-party compliance roles.

proposed_title: Develop and resolve environmental enforcement cases
description: Build cases from referral through penalty calculation, negotiation, consent orders, settlement or litigation support; testify as an expert or fact witness; prosecute citations where authorized.
rationale: State agencies run dedicated enforcement case-management roles (EGLE enforcement sections; MPCA compliance and enforcement unit). v1 6.1.5 is thin, has no case-to-settlement arc and has no testimony.

proposed_title: Operate and maintain drinking water or wastewater treatment systems in responsible charge
description: Operate treatment processes, interpret process control and laboratory data, respond to upsets, maintain equipment and SCADA, and meet permit and drinking-water standards as the certified operator in responsible charge.
rationale: Largest local public environmental workforce, wholly absent from v1 (0 mentions). Certification grades give a ready proficiency scale. Sources were not retrievable this session; DB and LM to supply evidence.

proposed_title: Assure public water system compliance
description: Track monitoring and reporting by public water systems, conduct sanitary surveys, manage Lead and Copper Rule and other rule compliance, and direct corrective action and public notification.
rationale: State primacy staff (EGLE Lead and Copper Compliance Analyst) perform this distinct regulatory function. No v1 competency covers drinking water compliance.

proposed_title: Conduct environmental public health inspections and plan reviews
description: Inspect food establishments, onsite wastewater (septic) systems, pools, housing and vector habitats; review plans; investigate complaints and outbreaks; apply sanitary codes under state registration or licensure.
rationale: CA requires REHS registration for some positions, TX runs a Sanitarian series, and FL state and county classes require pest-control and food-safety credentials. v1 F13 is EJ-centred and has no inspection practice.

proposed_title: Conduct environmental review under state and federal environmental policy acts
description: Scope, prepare, review or supervise environmental documents under state acts (CEQA, SEPA, MEPA, SEQRA and others) and NEPA, including joint or assigned documents, and keep the decision record defensible in each regime.
rationale: v1 6.1.4 is 'NEPA process implementation'. States staff entire units for their own acts (MPCA Environmental Review Unit) and DOTs run both regimes in one job (Caltrans). Generalize 6.1.4 with jurisdiction-specific enactments.

proposed_title: Oversee contaminated-site cleanup and remediation funds
description: Manage cleanup projects and contractors at brownfield, hazardous, Superfund-state-share and UST sites; review work plans and reports against standards; administer cleanup fund claims and cost recovery.
rationale: PA ECB and MI MUSTA postings show remediation project and fund administration as standing state roles. v1 has only hazmat awareness (4.4.4) and risk assessment (6.7.1).

proposed_title: Provide compliance and technical assistance to regulated entities and local governments
description: Design and deliver plain-language guidance, training and site assistance that helps regulated entities and local governments comply before enforcement is needed.
rationale: FL DEP and PA DEP classes name compliance assistance as core duties. v1 has education for the public (5.4) but none aimed at regulated parties.

proposed_title: Oversee local or delegated program delivery
description: Provide technical authority, review and approval over county, municipal or district staff delivering state programs; audit performance; build local capacity.
rationale: WI DATCP specialists hold technical authority over county land conservation departments. State-local delegation is a core intergovernmental relationship that v1 frames only as coordination.

proposed_title: Administer environmental financial assistance to local governments
description: Run state revolving funds, grants and loans for water, wastewater, stormwater, solid waste and resilience projects: eligibility, priority lists, technical review, compliance with federal cross-cutters, closeout.
rationale: Large state function with no v1 home (v1 finance competencies are market and ESG oriented). Not evidenced this session; LM/DB to source.

proposed_title: Manage air emissions testing, monitoring and permitting programs
description: Review and approve stack test protocols and reports, certify continuous emissions monitors, run ambient networks, write operating permits and support state implementation plans.
rationale: v1 compresses all of air quality into one competency (6.7.5). WI Advanced 2 stack-testing roles and TX EPS V air modeling show distinct air sub-functions run by state and local air agencies.

proposed_title: Regulate solid waste and materials management facilities
description: Permit, inspect and enforce at landfills, transfer stations, recycling, scrap tire, grease and organics facilities; review financial assurance and closure plans.
rationale: v1 waste content (3.7) is circular-economy strategy; state and local work is facility regulation (FL, PA, MI postings).

proposed_title: Regulate oil and gas well environmental compliance
description: Inspect wells and sites; investigate gas migration, spills and water-supply complaints; review well transfer and plugging; prepare enforcement.
rationale: PA DEP Oil and Gas Program classes. Energy-extraction regulation is a large state environmental workforce absent from v1.

proposed_title: Practice within licensure scope and responsible charge
description: Know the scope-of-practice limits of one's license or certification (PE, PG, REHS, operator grade); work under or exercise responsible charge; seal, certify or refer work appropriately.
rationale: State classes are split by licensure (TX Engineering Specialist barred from PE duties; Geologic Specialist under a licensed P.G.; WI Act 111). Candidate for the transversal practice layer.

proposed_title: Map the decision authority and procedural pathway for a proposed action
description: Identify every institution with authority over a proposed action (federal, state, Tribal, local, private), the legal basis and the version of procedure that governs each, which decisions are sequential or concurrent, and where the critical path lies. Produce an authority map and pathway plan that others can act on.
rationale: With CEQ regulations gone, each agency has its own procedures, some of them easily changed handbooks, and they diverge most for multi-agency projects. Delegated programs can revert (Florida 404). Knowing which authority and which procedure version applies is now a core skill. This is v1's 'Institutional Landscape Literacy' (D6 Section 9), made observable.

proposed_title: Build and maintain a defensible administrative record
description: Document the reasons for decisions as they are made: the alternatives considered, how scope and effects boundaries were drawn, responses to substantive comments, consultation outcomes and the provenance of analyses, including AI-assisted content. Do this so a reviewing court, inspector general or successor can reconstruct why the decision was reasonable.
rationale: Under Seven County, courts give 'substantial deference', which makes the quality of the reasoned explanation the main defense. The CEQ action plan lists administrative record management among minimum functional requirements. PermitTEC links 761 NEPA cases to project records. AI drafting adds the need to track provenance.

proposed_title: Select, justify and document the appropriate level of environmental review
description: Screen a proposed action against agency-specific categorical exclusions and extraordinary circumstances, including adopting another agency's CE where allowed. Decide whether an EA or EIS is needed, apply statutory page and time limits, evaluate the Sec. 112 paid-acceleration option, and document the determination in structured form.
rationale: Review-level selection is where 2025-26 reforms hit hardest: CE consolidation and adoption, a plan-level CE (USDA-38d), deadlines and fees. Automated CE screening (Action Plan workflow automation; decision_element in the CEQ standard) moves human judgment to extraordinary-circumstance calls.

proposed_title: Direct and evaluate applicant- or contractor-prepared environmental documents
description: Set scope and standards for documents prepared by project sponsors or their contractors, check independence and adequacy, and document the agency's own evaluation before adopting them.
rationale: DOI keeps detailed CFR steps for applicant-prepared documents and requires bureaus to document their evaluation (Reclamation 2026). The sponsor-pays model (Sec. 112) adds to this. Agency staff shift from authoring to supervising, a different and assessable competency.

proposed_title: Supervise AI-assisted drafting and public-comment analysis for legal defensibility
description: Specify, check and sign off on AI-generated drafts and comment groupings. Sample and verify AI comment bins, find substantive and unique comments the model merged away, confirm that every substantive comment has a reasoned response, check citations and facts, and record what was AI-assisted.
rationale: CommentNEPA and SearchNEPA are in production, and WriteNEPA is in production/beta. DraftNEPABench estimates 1-5 hours saved per EIS subsection. SPEED would tie standing to 'substantive and unique' comments. The judgment about what a comment means legally is statecraft; general AI validation methods are DC (7.2.1). Coordinate with DC so this does not duplicate 7.2.1.

proposed_title: Design proportionate public engagement when participation is discretionary
description: Decide when, with whom and how to engage beyond legal minimums, based on legitimacy risk, affected interests, Tribal and community relationships, and litigation exposure. Document the rationale and close the loop with participants.
rationale: Under DOI's 2026 procedures, CEs and EAs require no public involvement, and EISs require only comment solicitation at the NOI. Engagement shifts from a compliance step to a judgment call that someone must make and defend. The UK standard 1.3 (Participation and Engagement) treats it as a leveled competency.

proposed_title: Negotiate permit conditions, mitigation and agreements using interest-based methods
description: Prepare for and conduct negotiations over permit conditions, mitigation, settlement terms or partnership agreements: separate interests from positions, build options, understand the alternatives to agreement, and turn agreements into terms that can be implemented.
rationale: Negotiation is the most researched teachable statecraft skill, but that literature (SC-050, SC-052) was not re-read this session, so this is [J]. ESA rule changes (harm, species-specific 4(d)) widen the room for negotiated outcomes. The competency is stable, while the instruments negotiated change.

proposed_title: Design and administer cross-jurisdictional stewardship agreements
description: Build and run master and project-level agreements (Good Neighbor, recreation GNA, co-stewardship, shared-stewardship MOUs, Tribal Forest Protection Act projects): scope work within legal limits on delegating inherent government functions, set revenue retention and reinvestment, assign roles and reporting, and keep the agreement alive through staff turnover.
subsector: public lands, forestry, recreation, watershed restoration
rationale: In FY2025 there were 540 GNAs (426 with states, 50 counties, 45 Tribes). Counties and Tribes may retain revenue through FY2028, the recreation GNA is new, Colorado HB26-1205 extends state authority to DOI, and a bill would allow 20-year agreements. Co-stewardship agreements are not self-funding and are limited by non-delegable functions.

proposed_title: Coordinate lead, cooperating and participating agencies to a shared schedule
description: Set up and run interagency roles, joint schedules and milestones (one-document approach, FAST-41 coordination plans and dashboard), resolve disputes about jurisdiction-by-law, and decide on or justify cooperating-agency requests.
rationale: The 2023 amendments codified one-document and lead-agency rules. SPEED would add cooperating-agency deadlines and county cooperating status. DOI allows reasoned denials of cooperating-agency requests. Dashboard milestones make schedule performance observable.

proposed_title: Formulate, justify and execute public budgets across appropriations cycles
description: Build and defend budget requests and justifications, run programs under continuing resolutions and shutdown contingencies, design cost recovery and fees, manage agreement-retained revenue and grant compliance, and connect spending to outcomes legislators and auditors will accept.
rationale: v1 covers only project budgeting (3.1.2). The UK Policy Profession Standards make Finance (2.3) one of eleven core standards. GNA revenue retention and Sec. 112 cost-based fees are 2025 fiscal instruments with direct workforce effects. Federal appropriations status for FY2026-27 was not verified this session.

proposed_title: Assess the durability and reversal risk of policy choices and time actions to policy windows
description: Judge how likely an instrument (rule, guidance, handbook, agreement, permit) is to survive changes of administration, litigation and budget cycles. Choose instrument types and timing accordingly, and prepare contingency plans for programs built on unstable instruments.
rationale: Agencies are moving procedures from regulation to nonbinding guidance and handbooks, which practitioners describe as 'more susceptible to changes in administration'. Florida 404 reverted to federal control. Durability judgment is the teachable core of what is usually called 'political savvy'.

proposed_title: Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance
description: Monitor rules, guidance, court decisions and legislation (AI-assisted). Judge which changes affect which programs, decisions and staff, issue dated change notices, and update procedures and training.
rationale: v1 classifies legislative tracking (6.4.5 T1) as V, which is correct for monitoring. Translating changes into operations is not automated: Reclamation produced a 2026 staff deck to explain new DOI procedures. The pace of 2025-26 change (30+ instruments in policy_landscape_2026.csv) makes this a standing function.

proposed_title: Conduct government-to-government consultation as an obligation to a sovereign
description: Plan and carry out consultation with Tribal governments as governments, separate from public engagement: early and pre-decisional, at the right level of authority, respecting Tribal processes and control over knowledge and data, and documenting how input changed the decision.
rationale: Placeholder. TN owns this content and may revise or reject it. Streamlined NEPA leaves consultation duties in place (Reclamation 2026). The Tribal-side competency (a Tribal government running its own consultation and regulatory programs) must be written by or with TN.

proposed_title: Operate within, or oversee, delegated and assumed regulatory programs
description: Administer a state or Tribal program that holds federally delegated or assumed authority (e.g., NPDES, Title V, CWA 404, TAS), or oversee one: meet the federal predicates for the authority, manage the oversight relationship and plan for reversion risk.
rationale: Florida's 404 authority reverted to the Corps after the D.C. Circuit (2026-03-27) found the ESA consultation behind the assumption deficient. WOTUS uncertainty pushes states and Tribes toward their own programs. This is the state permit writer's distinctive statecraft and has no v1 home.

proposed_title: Manage regulated-entity disclosure and compliance across divergent regimes
description: Determine which disclosure and reporting regimes apply to an organization (CA SB 253/261, EU CSRD after Omnibus I, remaining federal programs), build defensible processes, prepare for assurance, and manage regulator and investor relationships as rules change or are enjoined.
subsector: corporate sustainability and ESG; regulated industry
rationale: Federal disclosure is receding (SEC rescission proposed; GHGRP cuts proposed), while CA reporting starts 2026-11-10 and EU scope has narrowed. The regulatory-affairs role has become a matter of jurisdictional judgment as much as reporting.

proposed_title: Draft enforceable, implementable binding instruments
description: Write permit conditions, agreement terms, policy language and decision documents that are clear, within authority, measurable, enforceable and workable for the people who must carry them out. Test drafts against implementation and challenge scenarios.
rationale: AI produces first drafts quickly (DraftNEPABench), so value moves to specifying, testing and owning the binding text. Drafting is one of the most assessable statecraft skills, because work samples can be scored.

proposed_title: Assess litigation exposure and design decisions for resilience on remand
description: Identify the claims a decision is likely to face under current deference, remedy and standing doctrine. Decide where more analysis or engagement reduces risk, and structure the record and decision so that a remand can be completed without restarting the project.
rationale: Seven County: a deficient EIS 'does not necessarily require vacating' approval. SPEED would mandate remand without vacatur within 180 days. PermitTEC records prevailing parties for 761 cases, a benchmark for calibrating risk judgment.

proposed_title: Brief decision-makers and elected officials for authoritative decisions
description: Prepare and deliver concise, candid briefings and staff reports for political principals and governing bodies (secretaries, governors, county boards, Tribal councils, commissions, corporate boards) that set out options, risks and recommendations, and give 'free and frank' advice under pressure.
rationale: UK standard 2.1 (Working with Ministers) levels this skill: from understanding ministerial pressures, to confident oral briefing, to being 'trusted ... to provide free and frank advice'. v1 spreads it across generic communication competencies.

proposed_title: Validate and assure AI-generated environmental analyses before decision use
description: Tests AI outputs against field ground truth, regulatory requirements and independent sources; documents error modes, fitness-for-purpose and residual uncertainty; decides when outputs may not be used.
rationale: Robust in all four scenarios (no-regret). v1 7.2.1 exists but is DC-only and lacks proficiency levels tied to decision stakes; expand into a full cross-family competency with observable indicators (IO).

proposed_title: Specify, test and monitor AI tools used in environmental decisions (model risk management)
description: Defines intended use, acceptance tests, performance monitoring and drift triggers for AI and models in permitting, enforcement targeting and monitoring; classifies high-impact uses.
rationale: OMB M-25-21 and agency AI strategies create the function; distinct from validating single outputs (FS-C01). Highest value in SC1 and SC3.

proposed_title: Maintain AI provenance and a defensible administrative record under accelerated review
description: Records data lineage, which analyses were AI-assisted, human review steps and responses to substantive comments so that records survive shorter deadlines and judicial review.
rationale: SPEED Act provisions (150-day limitations, substantive-comment requirement) plus AI drafting create a new failure point; speculative until courts address AI-assisted records.

proposed_title: Design and steward ground-truth reference data for Earth-observation and AI models
description: Plans field plots and labelled samples, maintains reference datasets and metadata, and runs regional validation to establish where models are fit for use.
rationale: EO foundation-model evidence shows labels and regional validation remain binding; gives field craft a durable role in AI-era monitoring (no-regret).

proposed_title: Fuse multi-source fire intelligence into operational decision support
description: Integrates satellite detections, cameras, weather, fuels and resource status into continuous situational awareness and briefings for initial attack, resource ordering and public warning.
rationale: FireSat early-adopter data from Q4 2026 and utility/state intelligence centers; connects to v1 WFIC/F16 work.

proposed_title: Plan and govern BVLOS and autonomous field operations programs
description: Designs drone and robotic monitoring programs: concept of operations, airspace and safety management, data pipelines, maintenance and crew qualification.
rationale: Program-level competency distinct from piloting (v1 4.5.4); timing contingent on Part 108 final rule.

proposed_title: Verify environmental claims using digital MRV with field calibration
description: Audits remote-sensing and sensor-based estimates, dynamic baselines and uncertainty; designs targeted field sampling to calibrate and challenge digital estimates; judges additionality and permanence claims digital data cannot prove.
rationale: Verification is platformizing; competency keeps human judgment where digital evidence is weakest.

proposed_title: Calibrate assessor judgment and measure inter-rater reliability in field assessments
description: Runs calibration exercises, measures agreement between assessors, and adjusts protocols so condition scores, surveys and credit metrics reflect real ecological change.
rationale: Assessor variability alone can generate a 10% BNG uplift; the same skill underpins defensible EMST tagging (IO lane).

proposed_title: Own and steward a public environmental technology product
description: Applies product management to case-management, permitting and monitoring systems: user research with practitioners, backlog and roadmap, data-standard compliance, adoption and change management.
rationale: CEQ data standard and Innovation Center create the need; FAS/EPIC called for product managers; agencies rarely have this role.

proposed_title: Procure and manage environmental technology and data contracts that protect public data rights
description: Writes requirements, evaluates vendors, negotiates data ownership, model access, auditability and exit terms, and manages performance of technology and data-service contracts.
rationale: Critical in Platform Stewardship (SC3) where public agencies become intelligent customers of private and philanthropic data; useful everywhere.

proposed_title: Steward an environmental digital twin across its lifecycle
description: Maintains data assimilation, validation under nonstationary conditions, uncertainty communication, access governance and retirement decisions for operational digital twins.
rationale: Watch-state candidate: v1 2.7.3 covers development but not operational stewardship; operational demand 5-10y.

proposed_title: Elicit, document and transfer tacit field and institutional knowledge before cohort exit
description: Uses structured interviews, paired fieldwork, after-action reviews and recorded field walks to transfer place-based and institutional knowledge from departing experts; respects Indigenous knowledge governance.
rationale: EPA departing median tenure 30.3 years; robust in all scenarios; urgent in SC4. Tribal knowledge only on holders' terms (TN).

proposed_title: Design AI-augmented apprenticeships that preserve the learning substrate
description: Redesigns entry-level work so juniors still produce, field-check and defend analyses while using AI; measures learning outcomes as well as throughput.
rationale: Directly counters v1 CLD signals; v1 7.2.2 is the seed. Robust across scenarios (no-regret).

proposed_title: Negotiate and administer intergovernmental stewardship agreements
description: Structures and manages co-stewardship, Good Neighbor, self-governance (638) and state-based leadership agreements: authorities, funding, performance and dispute resolution.
rationale: Devolution and Tribal assertion of governmental roles make agreement craft central; v1 splits it across 6.5.x without agreement lifecycle management.

proposed_title: Scan horizons and translate weak signals into workforce decisions
description: Monitors signals, maintains scenarios, runs foresight sessions and converts findings into no-regret and contingent workforce moves with triggers.
rationale: Distinguish from 6.2.5 (policy scenario analysis) and 1.7.5 (ecological non-analog futures); needed by EMST's own sentinels and by workforce planners.

proposed_title: Translate climate-risk data into navigable adaptation options for communities
description: Turns hazard, exposure and funding information into options small jurisdictions and households can act on; brokers technical assistance as federal support thins.
rationale: Speculative role signal; confirm with state/local posting data (SL, IA).

proposed_title: Design domain tasks and grading rubrics for evaluating environmental AI
description: Creates realistic multi-step environmental work tasks, reference answers and rubrics used to train, test and red-team AI agents.
rationale: Paid market already exists (Jun 2026); same skill supports agency acceptance testing (FS-C02).

proposed_title: Prepare assurance-ready GHG and nature disclosures across divergent regimes
description: Builds auditable inventories and nature metrics that satisfy SB 253, ESRS and ISSB-aligned requirements simultaneously; manages assurance.
rationale: v1 3.6.2 names GRI/SASB/TCFD (TCFD now absorbed into ISSB): rewrite around durable function, tools/frameworks in tool layer (DC lane).

proposed_title: Apply the federal trust responsibility and treaty-reserved rights to environmental and land management decisions
description: Identifies which Tribal nations hold treaty-reserved, statutory or Executive-order rights (hunting, fishing, gathering, water, access) in a project or planning area; analyzes how proposed actions affect the exercise of those rights; and designs measures that accommodate them. Observable: written rights analysis in the decision record; plan components that provide access and avoid restricting treaty uses except under the applicable legal test.
subsector: cross-subsector (land, water, fisheries, wildlife, energy siting)
rationale: Plans already require it: 102 treaty/reserved-right components in 39 plans, e.g., NWFP Aquatic Conservation Strategy 1994 'American Indian Uses' restriction test; Nez Perce-Clearwater 2025 FW-DC-TT-09 access for treaty-reserved rights. v1 mentions treaty rights only in a sector note. This is knowledge about federal law and obligations, appropriate for the project to define.

proposed_title: Conduct government-to-government consultation with Tribal nations as a pre-decisional process
description: Determines when an action has Tribal implications; invites Tribal leadership early, with adequate notice and materials, and with officials who hold decision authority present; seeks consensus where policy requires; keeps and shares a record of consultation; explains how Tribal input changed or did not change the decision; continues consultation through implementation. Observable: consultation plan, invitation timing, attendance of decision-makers, record shared with the Tribe, response-to-input documentation.
rationale: Rewrite of 6.5.1 with observable behaviors drawn from current agency policy (NPS DO 71C: 30-day notice, record within 10 business days; DOI 2022: early, pre-decisional, consensus-seeking, staff training before participation). Tribes in the 2025 USWFS consultation criticized webinars presented as consultation - the competency must distinguish consultation from notification. Transforming because procedural floors are moving (OMB M-25-36; Part 800 NPRM).

proposed_title: Protect confidential Tribal information across records systems, disclosure law and AI tools
description: Before receiving information from a Tribe, explains what records and disclosure laws (FOIA, state public-records acts) could compel the organization to release and what exemptions exist (e.g., NHPA s.304, ARPA) without overstating protection; withholds sensitive site locations from maps, reports and datasets; keeps Tribal information out of third-party AI and cloud tools unless the Tribe authorizes it; applies the Tribe's handling instructions. Observable: disclosure briefing documented; redaction/holdback log; AI-use authorization on file.
rationale: 301 DM 7 tells staff not to overstate confidentiality given FOIA limits; NPS will not record culturally sensitive information without permission; plans carry NHPA s.304 confidentiality standards (Mt Baker-Snoqualmie 1990; Umatilla 1990). v1 exposure coding treats documentation of Tribal input and cultural-site mapping as AI-augmentable without any governance condition, which makes this an emerging, AI-driven need.

proposed_title: Structure and administer agreements with Tribal governments for shared or Tribally led stewardship
description: Selects and uses the right instrument for the purpose - self-determination contracts and self-governance compacts (ISDEAA/P.L. 93-638), cooperative agreements, MOUs, co-stewardship and co-management agreements, Tribal Forest Protection Act and Good Neighbor agreements with Tribes, data-sharing agreements - and administers them so that Tribal authority, funding and decision roles are honored. Observable: agreement drafted with roles, authorities, funding and dispute terms; inherently federal functions correctly reserved; performance and payment on schedule.
rationale: Fire and forestry already run through 638 contracts and compacts (three options per NIFC Ch.6); 400 co-stewardship agreements existed by Dec 2024; USWFS must build ISDEAA administration capacity; Tribes asked for formal agreements and advisory structures. Transforming because the policy footing shifted in 2025-26 (EO 14112 rescinded; Bears Ears Commission eliminated).

proposed_title: Operate within Tribal jurisdiction and Tribal law as a non-Tribal party
description: Recognizes when Tribal law and Tribal regulatory authority apply (e.g., Tribal codes, Tribal water quality standards under treatment-as-a-state, Tribal permits and cultural resource ordinances on Tribal lands, Tribal research codes) and complies with them; coordinates with the Tribal department that holds the authority. Observable: Tribal requirements identified in project scoping; Tribal approvals obtained where required.
rationale: v1 frames Tribes as parties to be consulted, never as governments whose law binds others. Tribal environmental programs build ordinances (e.g., Tribal air ordinance as an eligible CAA 103 activity; Tribal response program ordinances under CERCLA 128(a)). The July 2026 draft Part 800 would replace Tribal concurrence on Tribal-land discoveries with consultation, which makes knowing Tribal law more, not less, important. Label J because I did not read a source enumerating TAS approvals.

proposed_title: Support Tribally led cultural and prescribed fire as a partner without directing Tribal knowledge
description: Removes administrative and operational barriers to Tribally led burning on lands the organization manages (planning, permitting, liability, resource ordering, smoke coordination, reimbursements) under agreements with the Tribe; defers objectives, methods and knowledge to Tribal fire practitioners; ensures qualification requirements do not exceed what the agreement specifies. Observable: barriers documented and resolved; agreement-based burn plans; timely reimbursement.
rationale: Tribes asked USWFS for basic cultural burning protocols, a Tribal consultation section in regional fire management plans and reduced barriers to Tribally led prescribed fire; California's 2021 strategy created a grant program for Tribal cultural burning. Replaces v1's recommendation to credential Indigenous fire stewardship: the competency describes the partner's conduct, not the knowledge.

proposed_title: Govern data about Tribal lands, resources and peoples under Tribal authority (CARE alongside FAIR)
description: Identifies when a monitoring, research or analytics activity generates data about Tribal lands, resources, citizens or knowledge; establishes before collection, with the Tribe's data authority, who owns, accesses, publishes, retains and can withdraw the data; applies CARE alongside FAIR; uses Local Contexts Notices where appropriate; honors repatriation and deletion requests. Observable: signed data agreement predating collection; metadata carrying Tribal terms; withdrawal executed when requested.
rationale: Revision of 7.1.1 for non-Tribal professionals. Monitoring partnerships are a common co-stewardship form (Mashpee Wampanoag review of offshore wind environmental data). CARE and Local Contexts details are from prior knowledge (TN-060, TN-061 not re-read this session) - re-verify before publication. Publication gated on Tribal review (P-TN-03).

proposed_title: Administer federal or state funding to Tribal governments in ways that respect self-governance
description: Structures awards and agreements to minimize reporting burden, pays and reimburses on time, supports recurring and compactable funding where authorized, includes staffing costs in base funding, and involves Tribes in formula and budget development. Observable: payment cycle times; reporting requirements justified; Tribal input in formula design documented.
subsector: grants and financial assistance; fire; forestry; environmental programs
rationale: What Tribal employers asked for: reimbursement backlogs (about $8.6M Santa Ynez Band of Chumash since 2019; about $3M Karuk); 'project-by-project funding is not sustainable'; IFMAT IV: base funding should cover staffing at GS-equivalent pay before project funds grow; Congress members cite reporting burdens. This is the federal side of Tribal workforce stability.

proposed_title: Apply Indian preference and Tribal employment rights lawfully in hiring for positions serving Tribal lands
description: Knows where Indian preference applies (statutory federal preference for BIA/IHS; Tribal preference ordinances and TERO requirements on Tribal lands; preference provisions in self-determination agreements) and applies it as a political classification; designs recruitment so preference does not leave positions vacant (e.g., pathways for preference hires from other disciplines). Observable: compliant announcements; documented preference determinations; bridging training plans.
rationale: Tribes asked USWFS to apply Indian preference across roles serving Tribal lands as a political classification; IFMAT IV finding C4 notes preference hiring increased Native foresters but some positions go unfilled or hires need NASP preparation. Coordinate with FH (federal hiring) - I am not proposing FH's lane, only flagging the competency.

proposed_title: Engage with Indigenous knowledge only on its holders' terms
description: Recognizes that Indigenous knowledge belongs to and is interpreted by its holders; asks the Tribe's governance structure who may share knowledge and under what conditions; obtains free, prior and informed consent before receiving it; uses it only for the purpose agreed; attributes it as the holder specifies (including not at all); compensates time and services without claiming ownership; declines to characterize, summarize or generalize it beyond what is authorized. Observable: consent record; purpose limitation in agreement; attribution as specified; no unauthorized reuse.
rationale: Replaces v1 5.3.2. The competency concerns the professional's conduct, which is the project's to describe; it does not define or rank Indigenous knowledge. Drawn from 301 DM 7 (FPIC before receipt; rely on Indigenous Peoples to interpret; IK inalienable; compensation does not transfer ownership) and NPS DO 71C. Requires Tribal advisory review before publication.

proposed_title: Coordinate cultural resource work with Tribal Historic Preservation Officers under Tribal direction
description: Engages THPOs and Tribal cultural monitors early in identification, evaluation and effects work; refers determinations of religious and cultural significance to Tribes; protects confidential site information; plans for post-review discoveries consistent with Tribal law on Tribal lands; maintains working relationships beyond individual undertakings. Observable: THPO engaged before identification fieldwork; referrals logged; confidentiality maintained.
subsector: cultural resources; NEPA/Section 106; energy and infrastructure siting
rationale: Rewrite of 5.3.3 task language. 129 plan components carry NHPA Section 106 touchpoints. The July 2026 draft Part 800 rewrite (pending OIRA) would reduce THPO roles and remove Tribal special-expertise language; practitioners who keep THPOs engaged early will be operating above a lowered floor. Transforming because the regulatory baseline is changing.

proposed_title: Sustain government-to-government obligations when procedural requirements change
description: Tracks changes to consultation, Section 106 and NEPA procedures (e.g., OMB M-25-36 presumptions; Part 800 rulemaking; post-Seven County NEPA practice; reorganizations such as USWFS) and distinguishes what remains required by treaty, statute, trust responsibility and Tribal law from what is procedural discretion; advises decision-makers on legal and relationship risk. Observable: change briefings; decision memos that separate obligations from discretion.
rationale: 2025-26 shows high procedural volatility (EO 14112 rescinded; M-25-36; USWFS; Bears Ears Commission eliminated; Part 800 NPRM). Practitioners in all actors need to keep obligations distinct from procedures. Proponent-side view (Hunton, TN-042) sees efficiency gains; Tribal organizations (NATHPO) see loss of meaningful consultation - the competency is neutral on the policy but requires knowing both.

proposed_title: Establish and sustain core environmental program capacity for a Tribal government
description: Builds and maintains the administrative, financial, information-management, baseline-assessment, public-education, legal and technical capacities a Tribal environmental program needs to plan, implement and, where the Tribe chooses, assume federal environmental programs; develops and updates an EPA-Tribal Environmental Plan (ETEP); manages multi-media work across water, air, waste and land with small staff. Observable: ETEP current; workplans meeting commitments; programs assumed or implemented as planned.
rationale: The only candidate here written FOR Tribal employees rather than for non-Tribal partners. It describes public-administration functions defined in EPA's public GAP framework, not Indigenous knowledge, so it is within scope - but it must be validated by Tribal environmental professionals (e.g., via Regional Tribal Operations Committees, ITEP) and carried in a Tribal-actor role variant only if they agree it reflects their work. FY26 priorities emphasize delegated programs and solid/hazardous waste.
